title: Continuum confinement in pure SU(3) gauge theory
open: Why do isolated color charges never appear in the world described by pure SU(3) gauge theory? Prove confinement in an appropriately defined continuum pure SU(3) theory—for example, a positive asymptotic string tension for large Wilson loops—and connect that statement rigorously to the physical spectrum.
status: Wilson's lattice formulation dates to 1974 (Wilson, *Confinement of Quarks*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445). Strong-coupling expansions and numerical continuum extrapolations support confinement (Davoudi et al., 2022, *Report of the Snowmass 2021 Topical Group on Lattice Gauge Theory*, arXiv:2209.10758), but a general continuum proof is absent; a mass gap alone would not establish every confinement criterion.
solved_when: A rigorously defined continuum pure SU(3) theory is shown to be confining in a recognized sense, e.g. Wilson loops exhibiting area-law decay with a positive asymptotic string tension, with the result tied rigorously to the physical spectrum.
why: It would explain, rather than assume, why isolated color charges do not occur.
key_works: Kenneth Wilson, 1974, *Confinement of Quarks*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445; Davoudi et al., 2022, *Report of the Snowmass 2021 Topical Group on Lattice Gauge Theory*, arXiv:2209.10758.

title: Analytic solution of the three-dimensional Ising critical point
open: Can the three-dimensional Ising critical point be solved exactly — that is, can its scaling dimensions and operator-product coefficients be determined analytically, or derived from an exact constructive characterization of the critical theory?
status: Open since the three-dimensional Ising model became a central statistical model. Conformal bootstrap methods, notably El-Showk et al., 2012, *Solving the 3D Ising Model with the Conformal Bootstrap*, arXiv:1203.6064, yield exceptionally precise numerical constraints, but not an exact solution.
solved_when: The critical theory's scaling dimensions and operator-product coefficients are obtained analytically, or an exact constructive characterization of the theory is given from which they follow.
why: An exact solution would provide a rigorous benchmark for interacting quantum field theories and sharpen our understanding of universality.
key_works: El-Showk et al., 2012, *Solving the 3D Ising Model with the Conformal Bootstrap*, arXiv:1203.6064.

title: Four-dimensional scale invariance versus conformal invariance
open: Does scale invariance imply conformal invariance for unitary, local, relativistic quantum field theories in four dimensions? The question is to prove this, or construct a counterexample, under explicitly stated spectral and stress-tensor assumptions.
status: The question has been studied for decades. Strong perturbative results and conditional arguments exist, but the fully general nonperturbative statement depends delicately on the hypotheses; see Yu Nakayama, 2015, *Scale Invariance vs Conformal Invariance*, arXiv:1302.0884.
solved_when: A proof that scale invariance implies conformal invariance holds for all unitary, local, relativistic four-dimensional QFTs under the stated assumptions, or an explicit counterexample satisfying those assumptions.
why: It determines whether scale-invariant phases can exist outside the conformal framework.
key_works: Yu Nakayama, 2015, *Scale Invariance vs Conformal Invariance*, arXiv:1302.0884.

title: Nonperturbative quantum gravity in de Sitter space
open: Define a nonperturbative quantum theory with positive cosmological constant and specify its observables, Hilbert-space interpretation, and semiclassical limit.
status: Proposed de Sitter holographic descriptions and lower-dimensional models exist, but no framework has achieved the completeness of well-understood anti-de Sitter examples.
why: Connects quantum gravity to a universe with accelerated expansion.
key_works: Andrew Strominger, 2001, *The dS/CFT Correspondence*, hep-th/0106113; Strominger, 2009, *Five Problems in Quantum Gravity*, arXiv:0906.1313.

title: Strong cosmic censorship at physically appropriate regularity
open: In what precise sense does general relativity predict a unique future? Formally, establish that the maximal globally hyperbolic development of generic initial data for the Einstein equations is inextendible at a specified regularity threshold, such as twice-differentiable metrics or finite-energy weak solutions.
status: Strong cosmic censorship is not one interchangeable conjecture: continuity-level formulations encounter counterexamples. Dafermos and Luk’s Kerr-interior work (arXiv:1710.01722; DOI: 10.4007/annals.2025.202.2.1) demonstrates why regularity thresholds matter.
solved_when: Generic inextendibility of the maximal globally hyperbolic development is proven at an explicitly stated regularity level (e.g., C² metrics or finite-energy weak solutions).
why: It pins down the exact sense in which Einstein’s equations determine the future uniquely, closing the gap that lets deterministic evolution fail inside black holes.
key_works: Dafermos and Luk, 2017/2025, *The Interior of Dynamical Vacuum Black Holes I: The C0-Stability of the Kerr Cauchy Horizon*, arXiv:1710.01722; DOI: 10.4007/annals.2025.202.2.1.

title: Stability islands and collapse in anti-de Sitter space
open: Which small perturbations of anti-de Sitter spacetime stay globally regular, which settle into quasiperiodic motion, and which cascade energy through scales until they collapse into a black hole? A complete characterization would partition perturbation space into stability islands and turbulent-collapse regions.
status: The 2011 weak-turbulence result of Bizoń and Rostworowski (arXiv:1104.3702) motivated extensive numerical and analytic work. Stable islands are known to exist, so "every small perturbation collapses" is not the correct target.
solved_when: A criterion (analytic or rigorously numerically supported) exists that classifies arbitrary small perturbations of AdS into globally regular, quasiperiodic, or turbulent-collapsing regimes.
why: It explains gravitational thermalization and delineates the true limits of perturbative stability of a maximally symmetric spacetime.
key_works: Bizoń and Rostworowski, 2011, *On Weakly Turbulent Instability of Anti-de Sitter Space*, arXiv:1104.3702.

title: Generic BKL behavior near cosmological singularities
open: Does a generic spacelike singularity in four-dimensional general relativity exhibit the local, oscillatory behavior conjectured by Belinski, Khalatnikov, and Lifshitz, and can this be proven or rigorously delimited? Formally, establish (or bound the scope of) the BKL picture — dynamics dominated by local, oscillating Kasner regimes — for solutions near generic spacelike singularities.
status: The original Belinski–Khalatnikov–Lifshitz arguments date to 1970. Rigorous and numerical results cover important symmetry classes — including work such as Hans Ringström, 2001, *The Bianchi IX Attractor* — but the generic inhomogeneous case remains incomplete.
solved_when: A rigorous proof (or a rigorous delimitation showing where it fails) of local, oscillatory BKL-type behavior for the generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularity in four-dimensional general relativity is established.
why: It would provide a predictive description of the classical approach to extreme curvature, telling us what general relativity actually predicts as spacetime curvature grows without bound.
key_works: Belinski, Khalatnikov, and Lifshitz, 1970, *Oscillatory Approach to a Singular Point in the Relativistic Cosmology*; Hans Ringström, 2001, *The Bianchi IX Attractor*.

title: Gravity-mediated entanglement experiment
open: Can gravity transmit a quantum resource — specifically, can entanglement be generated between two masses purely through their gravitational interaction, with all electromagnetic, mechanical, and measurement-mediated channels conclusively ruled out?
status: Concrete experimental proposals appeared in 2017, notably Bose et al., 2017, *Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.240401, and Marletto and Vedral, 2017, *Gravitationally Induced Entanglement between Two Massive Particles Is Sufficient Evidence of Quantum Effects in Gravity*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.240402. The central obstacle remains preparing, isolating, and controlling sufficiently massive spatial superpositions.
solved_when: An experiment observes entanglement between two massive objects attributable to their mutual gravitational coupling, with auxiliary tests excluding electromagnetic, mechanical, and measurement-mediated mechanisms as the source of the observed correlations.
why: A positive result would show that gravity can act as a genuine quantum channel, providing empirical evidence of quantum effects in the gravitational field rather than merely quantizing matter interacting with it classically.
key_works: Bose et al., 2017, *Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.240401; Marletto and Vedral, 2017, *Gravitationally Induced Entanglement between Two Massive Particles Is Sufficient Evidence of Quantum Effects in Gravity*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.240402.

title: Consistent measurement of Newton’s gravitational constant
open: Can independent measurements of Newton's gravitational constant be brought into mutual agreement with compatible uncertainty budgets, so that the remaining spread reflects genuine statistical scatter rather than uncontrolled systematics? In other words, can the persistent discrepancies be traced to identified, hidden systematic effects instead of being averaged away?
status: The measurement lineage begins with Cavendish, and modern methods still produce difficult-to-reconcile results; improvement is limited by systematic control rather than only statistical precision. Key works include Terry Quinn, 2014, *The Newtonian Constant of Gravitation—A Constant Too Difficult to Measure? An Introduction*, and Li et al., 2018, *Measurements of the Gravitational Constant Using Two Independent Methods*, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-018-0431-5. Related statistical issues concern combining measurements with unidentified systematic errors.
solved_when: Independent measurements of Newton's constant yield mutually compatible uncertainty budgets, with the discrepancy between results attributable to identified systematic effects rather than unexplained disagreement.
why: It resolves an unusually weak point in the measurement of fundamental constants: gravitation's coupling strength is known far less precisely than other constants, and the obstacle is systematic control rather than statistical precision.
key_works: Terry Quinn, 2014, *The Newtonian Constant of Gravitation—A Constant Too Difficult to Measure? An Introduction*; Li et al., 2018, *Measurements of the Gravitational Constant Using Two Independent Methods*, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-018-0431-5.

title: Time dependence of dark energy
open: Is the Universe's accelerating expansion a steady effect, consistent with a cosmological constant, or does dark energy evolve over time — possibly signalling modified gravitational dynamics?
status: DESI's 2025 second-release analysis found dataset-dependent preferences for evolving dark energy, not a settled discovery; combinations and model assumptions materially affect significance. Key work: DESI Collaboration, 2025, *DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and Cosmological Constraints*, arXiv:2503.14738.
solved_when: Observational data establish, at settled statistical significance and robustly across dataset combinations and model assumptions, whether cosmic acceleration is consistent with a cosmological constant or requires evolving dark energy or modified gravity.
why: A settled answer distinguishes fundamentally different explanations of cosmic acceleration, separating Einstein's cosmological constant from dynamical dark energy or altered gravitational physics.
key_works: DESI Collaboration, 2025, *DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and Cosmological Constraints*, arXiv:2503.14738.

title: Primordial tensor-mode detection
open: Can we detect the primordial gravitational-wave signature in the cosmic microwave background polarization, cleanly separating it from gravitational lensing, Galactic foregrounds, and instrumental effects?
status: Experiments have established increasingly strong upper bounds; foreground-cleaned primordial tensor detection remains distinct from detecting ordinary gravitational waves. Key work: BICEP/Keck Collaboration, 2021, *Improved Constraints on Primordial Gravitational Waves Using Planck, WMAP, and BICEP/Keck Observations through the 2018 Observing Season*, arXiv:2110.00483.
solved_when: A foreground-cleaned detection of a primordial tensor contribution to CMB polarization is achieved, with lensing, Galactic foregrounds, and instrumental systematics demonstrably separated from the signal.
why: Such a detection probes the energy scale and dynamics of the early universe.
key_works: BICEP/Keck Collaboration, 2021, *Improved Constraints on Primordial Gravitational Waves Using Planck, WMAP, and BICEP/Keck Observations through the 2018 Observing Season*, arXiv:2110.00483.

title: Particle identification of dark matter
open: Can we identify what dark matter is actually made of, through a nongravitational interaction or some other discriminating signature? More formally, the goal is to detect such a signal and quantitatively connect it to a specific dark-matter constituent and to the observed cosmic abundance.
status: Gravitational evidence for dark matter is extensive, and searches have excluded important regions of model space, but no universally accepted particle identification has been established. Key works: Boveia et al., 2022, *Snowmass 2021 Dark Matter Complementarity Report*, arXiv:2211.07027.
solved_when: A nongravitational interaction or other discriminating signature is detected that identifies a dark-matter constituent and quantitatively connects it to the cosmic abundance.
why: It determines what most of the gravitating matter in the universe is made of.
key_works: Boveia et al., 2022, *Snowmass 2021 Dark Matter Complementarity Report*, arXiv:2211.07027.

title: Axion abundance from strings and domain walls
open: Can we predict the post-inflationary QCD-axion abundance with controlled uncertainties despite the enormous separation between defect-core and cosmological scales? Formally, this requires a quantitatively reliable extrapolation of axion string and domain-wall network dynamics and their radiation spectra across all relevant scales.
status: Numerical simulations have advanced substantially, but extrapolation of string dynamics and radiation spectra remains a major source of uncertainty. Key works: Gorghetto, Hardy, and Villadoro, 2018, *Axions from Strings: The Attractive Solution*, arXiv:1806.04677; Marsh, 2016, arXiv:1510.07633.
solved_when: A prediction of the post-inflationary QCD-axion relic abundance is obtained with controlled, quantified uncertainties that account for the extrapolation of string dynamics and radiation spectra across the separation between defect-core and cosmological scales.
why: It converts an axion cosmology into a reliable experimental mass target, telling experiments which axion mass to search for.
key_works: Gorghetto, Hardy, and Villadoro, 2018, *Axions from Strings: The Attractive Solution*, arXiv:1806.04677; Marsh, 2016, arXiv:1510.07633.

title: Higgs quartic self-coupling
open: Can we directly measure — or at least constrain in a model-independent way — the quartic self-coupling of the Higgs boson tightly enough to test its Standard Model value, rather than only permitting enormous deviations from it?
status: Triple-Higgs production, the relevant process, is exceptionally rare, and existing studies of higher-energy colliders establish possible channels only — no measurement has been achieved. A representative study is Dong et al., 2025, *Probing Triple Higgs Production via the 4τ2b Decay Channel at a 100 TeV Hadron Collider*, arXiv:2504.04037. Progress is tied to machine learning for reliable classification in extremely low-signal, high-background regimes.
solved_when: A direct or sufficiently model-independent constraint on the four-Higgs interaction is obtained that discriminates the Standard Model prediction from large deviations, via a demonstrated measurement channel (e.g., triple-Higgs production) rather than an established possibility.
why: The quartic coupling probes a region of the Higgs scalar potential that the trilinear coupling alone cannot access, testing the shape of electroweak symmetry breaking.
key_works: Dong et al., 2025, *Probing Triple Higgs Production via the 4τ2b Decay Channel at a 100 TeV Hadron Collider*, arXiv:2504.04037.

title: First-generation Higgs Yukawa couplings
open: Do the electron and the light quarks get their masses from the Standard Model Higgs, the same way heavier fermions do? Determining this requires measuring, or placing tight individual bounds on, the Higgs Yukawa couplings of the first-generation fermions.
status: Higgs couplings to heavier particles are much more accessible experimentally, while first-generation couplings remain especially difficult due to small rates and hadronic backgrounds. Key reference: Butler et al., 2023, *Report of the 2021 U.S. Community Study on the Future of Particle Physics*, arXiv:2301.06581.
solved_when: The electron and light-quark Higgs Yukawa couplings are each either measured or tightly constrained individually, at a level sufficient to test whether first-generation masses arise from the Higgs mechanism.
why: It tests whether a single mechanism gives mass to all charged elementary fermions, closing the largest gap in the experimental picture of the Higgs sector.
key_works: Butler et al., 2023, *Report of the 2021 U.S. Community Study on the Future of Particle Physics*, arXiv:2301.06581.

title: Strong-CP problem
open: Why is the CP-violating parameter of QCD so extraordinarily small when other interactions violate CP freely, and how could an explanation be tested experimentally?
status: The problem was formulated in the 1970s and remains open. Axions (Peccei and Quinn, 1977, *CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440; R. D. Peccei, 2008, *The Strong CP Problem and Axions*, hep-ph/0607268), special CP structures, and other constructions are viable research directions, not established solutions.
solved_when: A theoretical mechanism is established that accounts for the extreme smallness of the physical QCD CP-violating parameter, together with an experimental signature that distinguishes it from fine-tuning.
why: A solution could reveal new symmetries or particles beyond the Standard Model.
key_works: Peccei and Quinn, 1977, *CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440; R. D. Peccei, 2008, *The Strong CP Problem and Axions*, hep-ph/0607268.

title: Absolute neutrino mass scale
open: What is the absolute mass of the neutrino, measured directly rather than inferred from cosmological assumptions? The goal is a kinematic determination — for example, from the endpoint behavior of beta-decay spectra — of the neutrino mass scale, kept independent of cosmology-dependent bounds.
status: KATRIN's April 2025 result bounded the effective electron-antineutrino mass below 0.45 eV; this was a bound, not a positive mass measurement (KATRIN Collaboration, 2025 results announcement and associated analysis). The underlying measurement challenge is an inverse problem: extracting a tiny endpoint deformation in the presence of an uncertain instrumental response.
solved_when: A kinematic measurement determines the effective electron-antineutrino mass at a sensitivity reaching below the current bound of 0.45 eV, distinguishing a positive mass measurement from a mere upper limit.
why: A direct mass value would complete a missing piece of the particle mass spectrum and provide a sharp test of models of neutrino mass generation.
key_works: KATRIN Collaboration, 2025 results announcement and associated analysis.

title: Dirac or Majorana neutrinos
open: Are neutrinos their own antiparticles? A discriminating observation — lepton-number violation such as neutrinoless double-beta decay, or another signature — would settle whether neutrinos are Majorana or Dirac particles.
status: The Dirac–Majorana distinction has existed since the 1930s. Neutrino oscillations prove nonzero masses but do not distinguish Dirac from Majorana particles. Relevant work includes Ettore Majorana, 1937, *Teoria Simmetrica dell’Elettrone e del Positrone*; and Engel and Menéndez, 2017, *Status and Future of Nuclear Matrix Elements for Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay*, arXiv:1610.06548.
solved_when: An experiment or observation establishes, independently of nuclear-matrix-element uncertainties or other modeling assumptions, that neutrinos are Majorana or Dirac particles.
why: The answer reveals whether total lepton number is a fundamental symmetry of nature.
key_works: Ettore Majorana, 1937, *Teoria Simmetrica dell’Elettrone e del Positrone*; Engel and Menéndez, 2017, *Status and Future of Nuclear Matrix Elements for Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay*, arXiv:1610.06548.

title: Direct detection of the cosmic neutrino background
open: Can we directly detect the relic neutrinos left over from the early universe through an observable capture or other interaction signature, rather than inferring them indirectly from cosmological effects?
status: The relic neutrino background is a standard prediction of cosmology, but it has never been directly detected. Proposed capture methods face extremely small rates, endpoint backgrounds, and challenging energy resolution requirements.
solved_when: A detector registers a neutrino-capture (or comparable interaction) signal from the cosmic neutrino background that is statistically distinguishable from backgrounds such as beta-decay endpoint contamination.
why: A direct measurement would probe an epoch earlier than the cosmic microwave background, opening a window onto the universe within the first second that no other observation reaches.
key_works: Steven Weinberg, 1962, *Universal Neutrino Degeneracy*; Cocco, Mangano, and Messina, 2007, *Probing Low Energy Neutrino Backgrounds with Neutrino Capture on Beta Decaying Nuclei*, hep-ph/0703075.

title: QCD critical endpoint
open: Does the QCD phase diagram contain a critical endpoint at finite baryon density, and if so, where? A definitive answer requires locating any such endpoint with controlled theoretical and experimental uncertainties.
status: Heavy-ion fluctuation measurements and lattice expansions constrain the possibilities, but finite-density calculations and nonequilibrium effects still prevent a definitive identification of a critical endpoint.
solved_when: The existence or non-existence of a critical endpoint at finite baryon density is established, with any located endpoint accompanied by quantified theoretical and experimental uncertainties.
why: The answer determines the phase structure of strongly interacting matter — the map of how nuclear matter organizes itself under extreme conditions.
key_works: Mikhail Stephanov, 2009, *Non-Gaussian Fluctuations near the QCD Critical Point*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.032301.

title: Finite-density QCD sign problem
open: Can we compute finite-density QCD from first principles at physically relevant baryon densities? Formally: is there a controlled computational method whose cost remains useful as volume and precision increase, or can hard limits be established for specified algorithm classes?
status: Reweighting, imaginary chemical potential, Taylor expansion, complex contours, and other methods work in restricted regimes; there is no general practical solution. Key works include Troyer and Wiese, 2005, *Computational Complexity and Fundamental Limitations to Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170201, and Davoudi et al., 2022, arXiv:2209.10758.
solved_when: A general practical computational method for finite-density QCD exists that works at physically relevant baryon densities and whose cost remains useful as volume and precision increase; alternatively, rigorous limits are established for specified algorithm classes.
why: Unlocks first-principles dense-matter and phase-diagram predictions.
key_works: Troyer and Wiese, 2005, *Computational Complexity and Fundamental Limitations to Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170201; Davoudi et al., 2022, arXiv:2209.10758.

title: Unambiguous glueball identification
open: Can we identify a hadronic resonance and quantitatively establish that its structure is predominantly gluonic, once mixing with nearby quark–antiquark and multihadron states is properly accounted for? This is the quest for an unambiguous glueball assignment in the experimental spectrum.
status: Lattice calculations predict glueball spectra, and several experimental candidates exist, but mixing with other states and overlapping resonances complicate definitive assignment. Key works: Morningstar and Peardon, 1999, *The Glueball Spectrum from an Anisotropic Lattice Study*, hep-lat/9901004; Crede and Meyer, 2009, *The Experimental Status of Glueballs*, arXiv:0812.0600.
solved_when: A resonance observed experimentally is shown, with quantitative control over mixing with quark–antiquark and multihadron components, to have predominantly gluonic structure.
why: It would provide the most direct bound-state test of the self-interaction of non-Abelian gauge fields.
key_works: Morningstar and Peardon, 1999, *The Glueball Spectrum from an Anisotropic Lattice Study*, hep-lat/9901004; Crede and Meyer, 2009, *The Experimental Status of Glueballs*, arXiv:0812.0600.

title: QCD conformal-window boundary
open: Where does the conformal window end? For a given gauge group and fermion representation, determine the critical number of fermion flavors below which the theory confines and breaks chiral symmetry, and above which it flows to an infrared-conformal fixed point.
status: Perturbation theory controls part of the high-flavor regime (Banks and Zaks, 1982, *On the Phase Structure of Vector-Like Gauge Theories with Massless Fermions*), and lattice studies constrain individual theories (Appelquist, Fleming, and Neil, 2008, *Lattice Study of the Conformal Window in QCD-Like Theories*), but the boundary is not fully mapped.
solved_when: For specified gauge groups and fermion representations, the flavor-number boundary separating infrared conformality from confinement/chiral symmetry breaking is determined.
why: A solution would test our understanding of strongly coupled renormalization-group dynamics and inform composite-model possibilities built from near-conformal gauge theories.
key_works: Banks and Zaks, 1982, *On the Phase Structure of Vector-Like Gauge Theories with Massless Fermions*; Appelquist, Fleming, and Neil, 2008, *Lattice Study of the Conformal Window in QCD-Like Theories*.

title: Reliable neutrinoless-double-beta nuclear matrix elements
open: Can the nuclear matrix elements governing neutrinoless double-beta decay be calculated with uncertainties that are quantified, cross-validated across methods, and include many-body truncation, weak currents, and short-distance contributions?
status: Competing nuclear methods currently yield significant spreads in the matrix elements, and better calculations are essential even if an experimental signal is discovered; see Engel and Menéndez, 2017, *Status and Future of Nuclear Matrix Elements for Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay: A Review*, arXiv:1610.06548.
solved_when: Matrix elements for the relevant decays are computed with certified uncertainty budgets covering many-body truncation, weak currents, and short-distance contributions, and are cross-validated across independent nuclear-structure methods.
why: Reliable matrix elements are what turn a measured half-life into particle-physics information about the neutrino.
key_works: Engel and Menéndez, 2017, *Status and Future of Nuclear Matrix Elements for Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay: A Review*, arXiv:1610.06548.

title: Predictive low-energy fission fragment distributions
open: Can we predict how a nucleus splits in low-energy fission — the masses, charges, kinetic energies, and neutron multiplicities of the fragments — from first-principles theory with controlled uncertainties, rather than fitting distributions to data? The goal is a predictive framework valid for specified nuclei and incident energies.
status: Energy-density-functional and time-dependent approaches reproduce important trends but do not yet offer uniformly reliable predictions; see Schunck and Robledo, 2016, *Microscopic Theory of Nuclear Fission: A Review*, arXiv:1511.07503. A related mathematical perspective concerns rare transitions in high-dimensional dissipative systems.
solved_when: A theory delivers fragment mass, charge, kinetic-energy, and neutron-emission distributions for specified nuclei and incident energies, with quantified, controlled uncertainties rather than purely fitted distributions.
why: Reliable predictions feed directly into reactor modeling, waste characterization, and astrophysical reaction networks.
key_works: Schunck and Robledo, 2016, *Microscopic Theory of Nuclear Fission: A Review*, arXiv:1511.07503.

title: Stellar-energy carbon-12 alpha-capture rate
open: What is the rate of the \(^{12}\mathrm{C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}\mathrm{O}\) reaction at the energies relevant to helium burning in stars? A determination is needed with sufficiently small and defensible uncertainties at these stellar energies.
status: Direct measurements at stellar energies are extremely difficult, so the rate must be extrapolated, and this extrapolation depends on interference effects and subthreshold nuclear states. deBoer et al., 2017, *The \(^{12}\mathrm{C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}\mathrm{O}\) Reaction and Its Implications for Stellar Helium Burning*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.89.035007, reviews the problem; low-energy extrapolation is constrained by reaction theory.
solved_when: The reaction rate at helium-burning energies is determined with small, quantified, defensible uncertainties, sufficient to constrain extrapolations from direct measurements to stellar energy.
why: The rate sets the cosmic carbon-to-oxygen balance and influences subsequent stellar evolution, so its uncertainty propagates into predictions of stellar outcomes.
key_works: deBoer et al., 2017, *The \(^{12}\mathrm{C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}\mathrm{O}\) Reaction and Its Implications for Stellar Helium Burning*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.89.035007.

title: Cold dense-matter equation of state
open: What is the pressure–density relation and composition of matter inside neutron stars, and do phase transitions occur at densities reachable in those stars? Formally, this asks for the cold dense-matter equation of state, including its possible non-smooth features at accessible densities.
status: Current mass, radius, tidal, and nuclear measurements constrain the pressure–density relation, but they do not identify a unique equation of state. A key reference is Lattimer and Prakash, 2016, *The Equation of State of Hot, Dense Matter and Neutron Stars*, arXiv:1512.07820.
solved_when: The equation of state — the pressure–density relation and composition of cold dense matter, including the presence or absence of phase transitions at accessible densities — is determined uniquely, consistent with the existing mass, radius, tidal, and nuclear measurements.
why: It probes matter at densities unavailable in stable terrestrial samples, giving access to a regime of physics no laboratory experiment can reach.
key_works: Lattimer and Prakash, 2016, *The Equation of State of Hot, Dense Matter and Neutron Stars*, arXiv:1512.07820.

title: Hyperon puzzle
open: How can matter containing hyperons — which should become energetically favored at high density — remain stiff enough to support the observed heaviest neutron stars, or are hyperons in fact suppressed in their interiors?
status: The tension has sharpened with massive pulsar measurements. Repulsive interactions and phase transitions offer candidate resolutions, not a uniquely established composition. Key work: Chatterjee and Vidaña, 2016, *Do Hyperons Exist in the Interior of Neutron Stars?*, arXiv:1510.06306.
solved_when: A microscopic treatment of dense matter with strange baryons either yields an equation of state that supports the observed heavy neutron stars (with hyperons present), or a demonstrated mechanism is established that suppresses hyperons so that standard stiff equations of state are recovered.
why: A resolution ties poorly measured many-body interactions involving strange baryons directly to compact-star structure, turning mass and radius observations into probes of strange nuclear interactions.
key_works: Chatterjee and Vidaña, 2016, *Do Hyperons Exist in the Interior of Neutron Stars?*, arXiv:1510.06306.

title: Color superconductivity in nature
open: Does the quark matter inside compact stars actually enter a color-superconducting phase, and can we find an observable signature that would tell it apart from other possible compositions?
status: Pairing is theoretically compelling at asymptotically high density, but the relevant phases at neutron-star densities and their observable consequences remain uncertain. Key works: Alford, Rajagopal, Schäfer, and Schmitt, 2008, *Color Superconductivity in Dense Quark Matter*, arXiv:0709.4635.
solved_when: Color superconducting quark matter is either established or ruled out in compact objects, and a distinguishing observable signature is identified that separates it from competing compositions.
why: A positive answer would reveal an entirely new macroscopic quantum state of matter occurring in nature.
key_works: Alford, Rajagopal, Schäfer, and Schmitt, 2008, *Color Superconductivity in Dense Quark Matter*, arXiv:0709.4635.

title: Predictive core-collapse supernova explodability
open: Can we predict, from a star's pre-collapse structure alone, whether it will explode as a core-collapse supernova — and if so, with what explosion energy and what compact remnant? A successful theory would require no adjustable explosion prescriptions fitted to observed outcomes.
status: Multidimensional neutrino-radiation simulations now produce successful explosions for many progenitors, but the outcomes depend sensitively on progenitor structure, neutrino transport, turbulence, and microphysics, so no fully predictive, prescription-free mapping is yet available. Key works: Woosley and Janka, 2005/2006, *The Physics of Core-Collapse Supernovae*, astro-ph/0601261; Boccioli and Roberti, 2024, *The Physics of Core-Collapse Supernovae: Explosion Mechanism and Explosive Nucleosynthesis*.
solved_when: A predictive criterion or model maps initial stellar structure directly to explosion outcome (explosion vs. black-hole formation), explosion energy, and remnant type, validated against multidimensional simulations and without tunable explosion parameters.
why: It would explain the observed populations of neutron stars and black holes, and the chemical enrichment pattern produced by explosive nucleosynthesis.
key_works: Woosley and Janka, 2005/2006, *The Physics of Core-Collapse Supernovae*, astro-ph/0601261; Boccioli and Roberti, 2024, *The Physics of Core-Collapse Supernovae: Explosion Mechanism and Explosive Nucleosynthesis*.

title: Fast-radio-burst emission mechanism
open: What physical process produces the coherent radio emission of fast radio bursts, and where in the source environment does it occur? A complete answer must explain the observed polarization, spectra, temporal structure, and environmental dependence.
status: Magnetars are linked to at least some bursts, but identifying a source class does not settle the coherent-emission physics or population diversity. A comprehensive reference is Bing Zhang, 2023, *The Physics of Fast Radio Bursts*, arXiv:2212.03972; DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.035005.
solved_when: A coherent radiation mechanism and emission location are identified that account for the bursts' polarization, spectra, temporal structure, and environmental dependence.
why: It would explain one of the most extreme coherent electromagnetic phenomena known.
key_works: Bing Zhang, 2023, *The Physics of Fast Radio Bursts*, arXiv:2212.03972; DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.035005.

title: Coronal heating energy budget
open: What actually heats the Sun's corona — and in what proportions? Determine the relative contributions of reconnection, waves, and other processes to coronal heating across quiet regions, active regions, and open-field environments.
status: The puzzle dates to the identification of the hot corona. Realistic simulations reproduce important features, but a quantitatively closed, general energy budget remains absent. Key works include Gudiksen and Nordlund, 2005, *An Ab Initio Approach to the Solar Coronal Heating Problem*, astro-ph/0407266; and Arregui, 2015, *Wave Heating of the Solar Atmosphere*.
solved_when: A quantitatively closed, general energy budget for coronal heating is established, specifying the relative contributions of reconnection, waves, and other processes across quiet regions, active regions, and open-field environments.
why: A solution would explain stellar atmospheres more generally and directly improve space-weather modeling.
key_works: Gudiksen and Nordlund, 2005, *An Ab Initio Approach to the Solar Coronal Heating Problem*, astro-ph/0407266; Arregui, 2015, *Wave Heating of the Solar Atmosphere*.

title: Parker magnetostatic problem
open: When a magnetic field is anchored at its boundary, does a smooth force-free equilibrium always exist, or can the line-tying topology force the formation of ever more singular current structures? Determine under which line-tied magnetic topologies smooth force-free equilibria exist, and when ideal evolution necessarily develops increasingly singular current structures.
status: Parker’s arguments motivated decades of work. Current results depend on topology, boundary conditions, and the distinction between true singularities and thin current layers. Key works include Eugene Parker, 1994, *Spontaneous Current Sheets in Magnetic Fields*; Pontin and Hornig, 2020, *The Parker Problem: Existence of Smooth Force-Free Fields and Coronal Heating*, DOI: 10.1007/s41116-020-00026-5.
solved_when: A characterization is given of the line-tied magnetic topologies for which smooth force-free equilibria exist, together with criteria deciding when ideal evolution instead develops increasingly singular current structures, distinguishing true singularities from thin current layers.
why: It decides whether magnetic braiding in the solar corona naturally supplies the dissipation needed for coronal heating.
key_works: Eugene Parker, 1994, *Spontaneous Current Sheets in Magnetic Fields*; Pontin and Hornig, 2020, *The Parker Problem: Existence of Smooth Force-Free Fields and Coronal Heating*, DOI: 10.1007/s41116-020-00026-5.

title: Sources of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays
open: What astrophysical sources accelerate cosmic rays to the highest energies observed? The task is to identify the dominant accelerator populations and determine their composition, injection spectra, and maximum energies, properly accounting for magnetic deflection of the particles' trajectories.
status: Anisotropy and composition measurements constrain candidate sources but do not yet provide a complete source census (Hillas, 1984, *The Origin of Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays*; Alves Batista et al., 2019, *Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies*, arXiv:1903.06714).
solved_when: A source census is established in which the dominant ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray accelerator populations are identified, with their composition, injection spectra, and maximum energies inferred in a way consistent with anisotropy and composition measurements and with magnetic deflection taken into account.
why: It identifies nature's most powerful particle accelerators.
key_works: Hillas, 1984, *The Origin of Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays*; Alves Batista et al., 2019, *Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies*, arXiv:1903.06714.

title: Air-shower muon deficit
open: Why do air-shower simulations underpredict muon-related observables in parts of the ultrahigh-energy data? A complete answer must separate genuine hadronic-interaction-model deficiencies from the effects of primary composition and detector response.
status: The discrepancy appears across multiple analyses, and its magnitude depends on energy and observable. Key work: Albrecht et al., 2022, *The Muon Puzzle in Cosmic-Ray Induced Air Showers and Its Connection to the Large Hadron Collider*, arXiv:2105.06148.
solved_when: A quantitative explanation of the muon deficit is given that accounts for its energy dependence and observable dependence across the affected analyses, with the discrepancy attributed among interaction models, composition, and detector effects in a way that can be tested against data.
why: The deficit biases cosmic-ray composition inference and limits the use of air showers as tests of hadronic interactions beyond accelerator energies.
key_works: Albrecht et al., 2022, *The Muon Puzzle in Cosmic-Ray Induced Air Showers and Its Connection to the Large Hadron Collider*, arXiv:2105.06148.

title: Relativistic-jet composition and acceleration
open: Where along a relativistic jet is magnetic energy actually converted into bulk motion and radiation, and are these jets made of electron–positron pairs or baryons? Answering this across source classes would pin down both the acceleration mechanism and the particle content of jets.
status: Imaging, polarization, spectra, and simulations constrain different regions but leave major degeneracies. Key work: Blandford, Meier, and Readhead, 2019, *Relativistic Jets from Active Galactic Nuclei*, arXiv:1812.06025.
solved_when: A determination of the energy-conversion region and the electron–positron versus baryonic composition of jets is established consistently across source classes.
why: It explains how compact objects transport energy over enormous distances.
key_works: Blandford, Meier, and Readhead, 2019, *Relativistic Jets from Active Galactic Nuclei*, arXiv:1812.06025.

title: Quantum PCP conjecture
open: Is it QMA-hard to approximate the ground-state energy of a local quantum Hamiltonian to within a constant fraction of the total interaction strength? More precisely, does the quantum PCP conjecture hold under its relevant formulation?
status: Open since the 2000s. The NLTS breakthrough and good quantum LDPC codes solve important neighboring problems, but not the quantum PCP conjecture itself. Key works: Aharonov, Arad, and Vidick, 2013, *The Quantum PCP Conjecture*, arXiv:1309.7495; Natarajan and Nirkhe, 2024, *The Status of the Quantum PCP Conjecture (Games Version)*, arXiv:2403.13084.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that approximating the ground-state energy of local quantum Hamiltonians within a constant fraction of the total interaction strength is QMA-hard under the relevant formulation.
why: A resolution would establish fundamental limits on how well the energy of quantum matter can be approximated, settling a central question about the hardness of approximating quantum many-body systems.
key_works: Aharonov, Arad, and Vidick, 2013, *The Quantum PCP Conjecture*, arXiv:1309.7495; Natarajan and Nirkhe, 2024, *The Status of the Quantum PCP Conjecture (Games Version)*, arXiv:2403.13084.

title: Area law for general two-dimensional gapped ground states
open: Does every two-dimensional local gapped Hamiltonian have a ground state whose entanglement entropy scales with the boundary of the region rather than its volume? If no such area law holds in full generality, what additional assumptions must be added to make it true?
status: One-dimensional results are much stronger, while higher-dimensional generality remains a major obstacle despite many tractable models. A key reference is Eisert, Cramer, and Plenio, 2010, *Area Laws for the Entanglement Entropy*, arXiv:0808.3773.
solved_when: A proof exists that a suitably specified general class of two-dimensional local gapped Hamiltonians satisfies an entanglement area law, or a precise characterization is given of the additional assumptions under which such a law holds.
why: It determines when efficient tensor-network descriptions of quantum many-body states should exist, since area-law states are precisely the ones such methods can hope to capture.
key_works: Eisert, Cramer, and Plenio, 2010, *Area Laws for the Entanglement Entropy*, arXiv:0808.3773.

title: Three-dimensional self-correcting quantum memory
open: Construct a physically realistic three-dimensional local system whose quantum-memory lifetime grows favorably with system size at nonzero temperature, without continuous active correction. In other words, can passive self-correction — rather than continual measurement and recovery — protect quantum information in three spatial dimensions?
status: Four-dimensional idealized models and constrained lower-dimensional constructions provide partial lessons; a practical three-dimensional solution remains unresolved. Key works include Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl, and Preskill, 2002, *Topological Quantum Memory*, quant-ph/0110143, and Haah, 2011, *Local Stabilizer Codes in Three Dimensions without String Logical Operators*, arXiv:1101.1962.
solved_when: A physically realistic three-dimensional local system is constructed whose quantum-memory lifetime at nonzero temperature grows with system size and requires no continuous active correction.
why: A solution could radically reduce the overhead of quantum storage, replacing active error-correction machinery with the system's own passive dynamics.
key_works: Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl, and Preskill, 2002, *Topological Quantum Memory*, quant-ph/0110143; Haah, 2011, *Local Stabilizer Codes in Three Dimensions without String Logical Operators*, arXiv:1101.1962.

title: Practical fault tolerance with quantum LDPC codes
open: Can a complete architecture be built that performs useful logical computation with quantum LDPC codes under realistic constraints — restricted connectivity, leakage, correlated noise, and real-time decoding latency? In other words, can the asymptotic coding-theory advantage be carried through every layer of an actual physical machine?
status: The existence of asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes is solved, following Panteleev and Kalachev, 2022, *Asymptotically Good Quantum and Locally Testable Classical LDPC Codes*, arXiv:2111.03654, with related progress in Bravyi et al., 2024, *High-Threshold and Low-Overhead Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory*, arXiv:2308.07915. Translating these coding advantages into a robust physical machine remains a separate, open engineering problem.
solved_when: A working end-to-end architecture exists that implements useful logical computation with quantum LDPC codes while meeting the realistic hardware constraints listed above: connectivity, leakage, correlated noise, and decoding latency.
why: Such an architecture could substantially reduce the physical-qubit overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computing, which is currently the dominant cost of scaling machines.
key_works: Panteleev and Kalachev, 2022, *Asymptotically Good Quantum and Locally Testable Classical LDPC Codes*, arXiv:2111.03654; Bravyi et al., 2024, *High-Threshold and Low-Overhead Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory*, arXiv:2308.07915.

title: Exact quantum capacity of the depolarizing channel
open: What is the exact quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel in the noise range where current bounds disagree — and can degenerate codes, or improvements to them, close the gap between the known upper and lower bounds?
status: Decades of upper and lower bounds leave a gap between them; the single-letter coherent information is known not to be the full answer in general. The key work is DiVincenzo, Shor, and Smolin, 1998, *Quantum-Channel Capacity of Very Noisy Channels*, quant-ph/9706061.
solved_when: The quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel is determined exactly (upper and lower bounds coincide) throughout the previously unresolved noise range, including a resolution of whether degenerate codes close the existing bounds.
why: The depolarizing channel is the canonical noise model in quantum communication, so an exact capacity would provide a basic benchmark for all quantum communication protocols.
key_works: DiVincenzo, Shor, and Smolin, 1998, *Quantum-Channel Capacity of Very Noisy Channels*, quant-ph/9706061.

title: Nuclear-clock accuracy beyond first demonstrations
subfield: Atomic, molecular, and precision measurement physics
open: Can the thorium-229 nuclear transition be developed into a fully functioning clock with a complete uncertainty budget, reproducible long-term operation, and demonstrated advantages over leading electronic clocks?
status: Nuclear excitation and initial clock demonstrations are already milestones, not open targets; what remains unfinished is controlling solid-state or trapped-ion shifts and readout. Key works: Peik et al., 2021, *Nuclear Clocks for Testing Fundamental Physics*; Zhang et al., 2024, *Frequency Ratio of the \(^{229m}\)Th Nuclear Isomeric Transition and the \(^{87}\)Sr Atomic Clock*.
solved_when: A thorium-229 nuclear clock is operated with a complete, traceable uncertainty budget and reproducible long-term performance, and shows demonstrated advantages over leading electronic clocks.
why: It would open precision tests of fundamental physics and potentially new clock architectures.
key_works: Peik et al., 2021, *Nuclear Clocks for Testing Fundamental Physics*; Zhang et al., 2024, *Frequency Ratio of the \(^{229m}\)Th Nuclear Isomeric Transition and the \(^{87}\)Sr Atomic Clock*.

title: Electron electric dipole moment
subfield: Atomic, molecular, and precision measurement physics
open: Can we detect a nonzero electric dipole moment of the electron, or else rule out additional well-defined CP-violating model space using measurements in independent molecular or atomic systems?
status: Experiments have reached extraordinarily small upper limits without an accepted positive detection; key works include the ACME Collaboration, 2018, *Improved Limit on the Electric Dipole Moment of the Electron*, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-018-0599-8; and Roussy et al., 2023, *An Improved Bound on the Electron’s Electric Dipole Moment*, DOI: 10.1126/science.adg4084. Related progress depends on accurate relativistic electronic structure calculations for heavy polar molecules.
solved_when: Either a positive, reproducible detection of an electron electric dipole moment is announced, or new measurements in independent molecular or atomic systems exclude further well-defined CP-violating model parameter space beyond current limits.
why: It probes new sources of CP violation at energy scales beyond the direct reach of colliders.
key_works: ACME Collaboration, 2018, *Improved Limit on the Electric Dipole Moment of the Electron*, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-018-0599-8; Roussy et al., 2023, *An Improved Bound on the Electron’s Electric Dipole Moment*, DOI: 10.1126/science.adg4084.

title: Molecular parity-violating energy difference
subfield: Atomic, molecular, and precision measurement physics
open: Can we measure the tiny energy difference between left- and right-handed enantiomers of a chiral molecule that is predicted by electroweak parity violation, in a way that survives scrutiny of molecular-structure and instrumental systematics?
status: The effect has been predicted for decades and is extremely small; it has motivated increasingly sophisticated spectroscopy. Key works include Martin Quack, 2002, *How Important Is Parity Violation for Molecular and Biomolecular Chirality?* and Quack, Stohner, and Willeke, 2008, *High-Resolution Spectroscopic Studies and Theory of Parity Violation in Chiral Molecules*.
solved_when: A measured parity-violating energy splitting between enantiomers is reported with a signal robust against molecular-structure and instrumental checks; no numerical precision target is stated in the record.
why: It would provide a direct experimental link between the weak interaction and molecular handedness, a connection invoked in discussions of the origin of biological homochirality.
key_works: Martin Quack, 2002, *How Important Is Parity Violation for Molecular and Biomolecular Chirality?*; Quack, Stohner, and Willeke, 2008, *High-Resolution Spectroscopic Studies and Theory of Parity Violation in Chiral Molecules*.

title: Picogram matter-wave interferometry
subfield: Atomic, molecular, and precision measurement physics
open: Can we place a picogram-scale object into a spatially separated superposition of its center-of-mass and observe interference? Formally, this means demonstrating verified center-of-mass interference at picogram mass — a proposed mass-scale milestone rather than an existing record claim.
status: Molecular interferometry and levitated systems have advanced, but scaling to such masses requires simultaneous control of vibration, thermal emission, collisions, and preparation. Key works: Fein et al., 2019, *Quantum Superposition of Molecules beyond 25 kDa*; Bassi et al., 2013, arXiv:1204.4325.
solved_when: A center-of-mass interference signal from an object of picogram-scale mass is demonstrated, with the spatial separation of the superposition verified.
why: It would test whether quantum coherence survives in substantially more massive objects than anything interfered to date, probing the boundary between quantum and classical matter.
key_works: Fein et al., 2019, *Quantum Superposition of Molecules beyond 25 kDa*; Bassi et al., 2013, arXiv:1204.4325.

title: Atom-interferometric gravitational-wave observatory
subfield: Atomic, molecular, and precision measurement physics
open: Build an atom-interferometer observatory that achieves an astrophysically useful strain sensitivity in its intended frequency band under realistic laser, gravity-gradient, and environmental noise.
status: Long-baseline proposals and prototypes exist, including Graham et al., 2013, *New Method for Gravitational Wave Detection with Atomic Sensors*, arXiv:1206.0818, and the MAGIS-100 Collaboration, 2021, *Matter-Wave Atomic Gradiometer Interferometric Sensor: MAGIS-100*, arXiv:2104.02835; full astrophysical sensitivity remains an integrated-system target rather than a demonstrated result.
solved_when: An operating atom-interferometric observatory demonstrates astrophysically useful strain sensitivity in its intended frequency band while laser, gravity-gradient, and environmental noise are present at realistic levels.
why: It would open gravitational-wave frequency bands lying between existing detector classes, which no current instrument covers.
key_works: Graham et al., 2013, *New Method for Gravitational Wave Detection with Atomic Sensors*, arXiv:1206.0818; MAGIS-100 Collaboration, 2021, *Matter-Wave Atomic Gradiometer Interferometric Sensor: MAGIS-100*, arXiv:2104.02835.

title: Superconducting phase of the two-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model
open: Does the two-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model truly exhibit d-wave superconductivity, and if so, over what doping range and with what pairing strength? More precisely, establish its thermodynamic phase diagram and the existence, extent, and strength of d-wave superconductivity in physically relevant doped regimes.
status: Numerical methods strongly constrain the competing stripe, magnetic, and pairing states, but finite-size, temperature, and method-dependent limitations persist. Qin et al., 2021, *The Hubbard Model: A Computational Perspective*, arXiv:2104.00064.
solved_when: A controlled determination of the thermodynamic phase diagram of the two-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model, identifying whether a d-wave superconducting phase exists, its extent in doping, and its strength in the physically relevant doped regimes.
why: It tests whether a minimal electronic model can explain high-temperature pairing, making it the benchmark question for the microscopic theory of cuprate-like superconductivity.
key_works: Qin et al., 2021, *The Hubbard Model: A Computational Perspective*, arXiv:2104.00064.

title: Microscopic origin of strange-metal transport
open: What microscopic mechanism produces the linear-in-temperature resistivity and associated transport observed in strange metals? A complete account should explain these phenomena across specified strange-metal compounds while incorporating momentum relaxation and the material-dependent energy scales that vary from system to system.
status: Quantum-critical, hydrodynamic, and incoherent-metal approaches each reproduce aspects of the phenomenology. A universal "Planckian bound" should not be assumed without hypotheses (Bruin et al., 2013, *Similarity of Scattering Rates in Metals Showing T-Linear Resistivity*; Hartnoll and Mackenzie, 2022, *Colloquium: Planckian Dissipation in Metals*, arXiv:2107.07802).
solved_when: A microscopic theory reproduces the linear-in-temperature resistivity and associated transport across specified strange metals, correctly accounting for momentum relaxation and material-dependent scales.
why: It would replace quasiparticle-based transport descriptions precisely where they fail, restoring predictive power over an entire class of correlated-electron materials.
key_works: Bruin et al., 2013, *Similarity of Scattering Rates in Metals Showing T-Linear Resistivity*; Hartnoll and Mackenzie, 2022, *Colloquium: Planckian Dissipation in Metals*, arXiv:2107.07802.

title: Superconducting order parameter of Sr2RuO4
open: What is the true superconducting order parameter of Sr2RuO4? A complete answer must specify the order-parameter symmetry, spin structure, and nodal topology in a way that reconciles the thermodynamic, magnetic, strain, and time-reversal-sensitive measurements.
status: Sr2RuO4 was discovered as a superconductor in 1994. The once-common simple chiral-p-wave assignment is not an adequate settled answer. Ramires and Sigrist, 2019, *Superconducting Order Parameter of Sr2RuO4: A Microscopic Perspective*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevB.100.104501.
solved_when: The order-parameter symmetry, spin structure, and nodal topology of Sr2RuO4 are determined, with a single assignment consistent across thermodynamic, magnetic, strain, and time-reversal-sensitive measurements.
why: It resolves a benchmark unconventional superconductor and settles whether Sr2RuO4 is a viable topological pairing platform.
key_works: Ramires and Sigrist, 2019, *Superconducting Order Parameter of Sr2RuO4: A Microscopic Perspective*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevB.100.104501.

title: Ground state of the spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet
open: Does the spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet with nearest-neighbor interactions have a gapped topological spin liquid as its thermodynamic ground state, or is the true ground state gapless or of some other kind? A definitive answer would settle the long-standing disagreement among numerical extrapolations.
status: Decades of work have narrowed the possibilities, but closely competing candidate states continue to challenge existing numerical methods. Key works: Yan, Huse, and White, 2011, *Spin-Liquid Ground State of the S=1/2 Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet*; Savary and Balents, 2017, *Quantum Spin Liquids*, arXiv:1601.03742.
solved_when: The thermodynamic ground state of the nearest-neighbor model is determined — gapped topological spin liquid, gapless state, or otherwise — with controlled numerical evidence that resolves the extrapolation disputes among competing candidate states.
why: The model is a canonical test of quantum frustration and fractionalization, so a settled answer would validate or overturn the theoretical tools used to describe fractionalized states of matter.
key_works: Yan, Huse, and White, 2011, *Spin-Liquid Ground State of the S=1/2 Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet*; Savary and Balents, 2017, *Quantum Spin Liquids*, arXiv:1601.03742.

title: Field-induced phase of α-RuCl3
open: What is the true nature of the field-induced state in α-RuCl₃, and do the claimed thermal signatures of that state actually require a Kitaev-related chiral spin liquid, or can they arise from more conventional physics?
status: Magnetic suppression and transport measurements reveal unusual behavior, but sample dependence and phonon contributions complicate interpretation. Key works: Kitaev, 2006, *Anyons in an Exactly Solved Model and Beyond*, cond-mat/0506438; Broholm et al., 2020, *Quantum Spin Liquids*, arXiv:1905.07040.
solved_when: The field-induced phase is experimentally characterized with its origin identified — specifically, whether the observed thermal signatures demand a Kitaev-related chiral spin liquid — with sample-dependence and phonon contributions to the measured signals disentangled.
why: A resolution tests whether non-Abelian fractionalization occurs in a real material, with implications for metrology in separating quantized thermal transport from parasitic heat channels.
key_works: Kitaev, 2006, *Anyons in an Exactly Solved Model and Beyond*, cond-mat/0506438; Broholm et al., 2020, *Quantum Spin Liquids*, arXiv:1905.07040.

title: Intrinsic spin-liquid response of herbertsmithite
open: Can the intrinsic magnetic response of the kagome layers in herbertsmithite be disentangled from the contributions of disorder and interlayer defects, so that we can decide whether the clean material is gapped and topologically ordered?
status: Continuum scattering supports fractionalized interpretations, but defects make the low-energy behavior difficult to assign uniquely. Key works: Han et al., 2012, *Fractionalized Excitations in the Spin-Liquid State of a Kagome-Lattice Antiferromagnet*; Broholm et al., 2020, arXiv:1905.07040.
solved_when: The low-energy excitations attributable to the kagome layers alone are isolated, with disorder and interlayer-defect contributions quantitatively accounted for, and the resulting intrinsic spectrum is shown to be either gapped with topological order or not.
why: It would establish whether an ideal frustrated kagome model is realized in actual quantum matter, bridging theory and experiment in frustrated magnetism.
key_works: Han et al., 2012, *Fractionalized Excitations in the Spin-Liquid State of a Kagome-Lattice Antiferromagnet*; Broholm et al., 2020, arXiv:1905.07040.

title: Unambiguous non-Abelian braiding of Majorana modes
open: Can Majorana zero modes be braided in the laboratory so that the resulting exchange operations demonstrably fail to commute, with fusion outcomes and parity behavior consistent with non-Abelian statistics and with trivial Andreev-bound-state alternatives ruled out?
status: Candidate signatures such as zero-bias peaks are not by themselves proof of Majorana non-Abelian statistics. Key works: Alicea, 2012, *New Directions in the Pursuit of Majorana Fermions in Solid State Systems*, arXiv:1202.1293; Beenakker, 2013, *Search for Majorana Fermions in Superconductors*, arXiv:1112.1950.
solved_when: An experiment implements exchange (braiding) operations on Majorana modes and verifies noncommutativity of the operations, the predicted fusion-channel and fermion-parity behavior, and excludes ordinary Andreev-state explanations for the observed signals.
why: It would establish the physical basis of a major topological-quantum-computing approach, where protected gates follow from the statistics of the modes themselves.
key_works: Alicea, 2012, *New Directions in the Pursuit of Majorana Fermions in Solid State Systems*, arXiv:1202.1293; Beenakker, 2013, *Search for Majorana Fermions in Superconductors*, arXiv:1112.1950.

title: Non-Abelian fractional Chern insulator
open: Can a non-Abelian fractional topological phase be realized and identified without applying a large external magnetic field? Success would mean observing convincing exchange statistics or an equivalent topological diagnostic of the non-Abelian order.
status: Fractional quantum anomalous Hall phases are already established milestones, but non-Abelian order and operational braiding remain stronger, separate targets. Key works: Bergholtz and Liu, 2013, *Topological Flat Band Models and Fractional Chern Insulators*, arXiv:1308.0343; Xu et al., 2025/2026, *Signatures of Unconventional Superconductivity near Reentrant and Fractional Quantum Anomalous Hall Insulators*, arXiv:2504.06972.
solved_when: A non-Abelian fractional topological phase is experimentally realized in the absence of a large external magnetic field, and its non-Abelian character is established through convincing statistics or equivalent topological diagnostics.
why: It would make anyonic physics more tunable and device-compatible, moving exotic statistics toward practical platforms.
key_works: Bergholtz and Liu, 2013, *Topological Flat Band Models and Fractional Chern Insulators*, arXiv:1308.0343; Xu et al., 2025/2026, *Signatures of Unconventional Superconductivity near Reentrant and Fractional Quantum Anomalous Hall Insulators*, arXiv:2504.06972.

title: Continuity of deconfined quantum critical transitions
open: Which of the candidate Néel–valence-bond-solid transitions are truly continuous, and which are instead weakly first-order, and what role does emergent symmetry play in deciding this?
status: The problem was proposed in 2004; large simulations reveal striking scaling alongside drifts that permit competing interpretations. Key works: Senthil et al., 2004, *Deconfined Quantum Critical Points*, cond-mat/0311326; Nahum et al., 2015, *Emergent SO(5) Symmetry at the Néel to Valence-Bond-Solid Transition*.
solved_when: A determination, backed by controlled theory or numerics, of which candidate Néel–valence-bond-solid transitions are continuous versus weakly first-order, including a characterization of the role of emergent symmetry.
why: It tests critical phenomena beyond conventional order-parameter theory.
key_works: Senthil et al., 2004, *Deconfined Quantum Critical Points*, cond-mat/0311326; Nahum et al., 2015, *Emergent SO(5) Symmetry at the Néel to Valence-Bond-Solid Transition*.

title: Almeida–Thouless transition in three dimensions
subfield: Statistical mechanics and nonequilibrium quantum matter
open: Does a short-range three-dimensional Ising spin glass undergo an equilibrium spin-glass transition in a nonzero magnetic field? In other words, does the Almeida–Thouless line predicted by mean-field theory survive in three dimensions?
status: Mean-field theory predicts an Almeida–Thouless line (de Almeida and Thouless, 1978, *Stability of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick Solution of a Spin Glass Model*), while finite-dimensional theory and simulations do not yield an uncontested settlement (Young and Katzgraber, 2004, *Absence of an Almeida–Thouless Line in Three-Dimensional Spin Glasses*).
solved_when: A rigorous argument, or an uncontested numerical/theoretical settlement, establishes whether an equilibrium spin-glass transition occurs in a short-range three-dimensional Ising spin glass at nonzero field.
why: It distinguishes competing pictures of how glassy states are organized in finite-dimensional systems.
key_works: de Almeida and Thouless, 1978, *Stability of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick Solution of a Spin Glass Model*; Young and Katzgraber, 2004, *Absence of an Almeida–Thouless Line in Three-Dimensional Spin Glasses*.

title: Thermodynamic stability of one-dimensional many-body localization
subfield: Statistical mechanics and nonequilibrium quantum matter
open: Do generic disordered interacting one-dimensional systems possess a stable many-body-localized phase that survives in the limits of infinite time and infinite system size, under clearly specified assumptions? Formally, the question is whether localization persists in the thermodynamic limit rather than being a long-lived but ultimately transient crossover.
status: Finite-size experiments and simulations show localization-like behavior, but rare thermal regions and long crossover scales complicate extrapolation to the thermodynamic limit. Key works include Abanin et al., 2019, *Many-Body Localization, Thermalization, and Entanglement*, arXiv:1804.11065; and Sierant et al., 2025, *Many-Body Localization: Current Status and Open Questions*.
solved_when: A proof or refutation, under explicitly stated assumptions on the disorder distribution and interactions, that generic disordered interacting one-dimensional systems do (or do not) exhibit a many-body-localized phase stable at infinite time and size.
why: It determines whether interacting quantum matter can robustly evade thermalization, or whether apparent localization is always destroyed on long scales.
key_works: Abanin et al., 2019, *Many-Body Localization, Thermalization, and Entanglement*, arXiv:1804.11065; Sierant et al., 2025, *Many-Body Localization: Current Status and Open Questions*.

title: Higher-dimensional localization and thermal avalanches
subfield: Statistical mechanics and nonequilibrium quantum matter
open: Can stable many-body localization survive in two or more dimensions in specified local models, or do thermal avalanches inevitably destroy it?
status: Avalanche arguments challenge the stability of higher-dimensional localization; finite experimental and numerical systems cannot directly settle the asymptotic behavior. Key works: De Roeck and Huveneers, 2017, *Stability and Instability towards Delocalization in Many-Body Localization Systems*; Abanin et al., 2019, arXiv:1804.11065.
solved_when: Either a specified local model in two or more dimensions is shown to support stable many-body localization, or it is proven that thermal avalanches necessarily destroy localization in all such systems.
why: It fixes the dimensional limits of nonthermal quantum phases.
key_works: De Roeck and Huveneers, 2017, *Stability and Instability towards Delocalization in Many-Body Localization Systems*; Abanin et al., 2019, arXiv:1804.11065.

title: Fourier’s law from deterministic microscopic dynamics
subfield: Statistical mechanics and nonequilibrium quantum matter
open: Can Fourier's law of heat conduction — normal transport with a finite, well-defined thermal conductivity — be derived rigorously from deterministic microscopic dynamics for a sufficiently broad and physically realistic class of interacting systems?
status: Exact and rigorous results exist only for selected stochastic or special models; generic deterministic systems remain difficult, especially in low dimensions. See Bonetto, Lebowitz, and Rey-Bellet, 2000, *Fourier's Law: A Challenge to Theorists*, math-ph/0002052.
solved_when: A rigorous derivation of Fourier's law, with finite conductivity, is established for a broad, physically realistic class of deterministic interacting systems, not merely special or stochastic ones.
why: It would derive a basic macroscopic transport law directly from microscopic mechanics, closing a foundational gap between deterministic molecular dynamics and continuum heat conduction.
key_works: Bonetto, Lebowitz, and Rey-Bellet, 2000, *Fourier’s Law: A Challenge to Theorists*, math-ph/0002052.

title: Exact structure of 2+1-dimensional KPZ universality
subfield: Statistical mechanics and nonequilibrium quantum matter
open: Can the KPZ universality class in two spatial dimensions be solved exactly — its critical exponents, scaling distributions, or some equivalent solvable characterization captured at strong coupling? More formally, is there an analytic determination of the exact structure of 2+1-dimensional KPZ universality?
status: One-dimensional KPZ is far more analytically developed, while higher-dimensional exponents are primarily numerical. Key works: Kardar, Parisi, and Zhang, 1986, *Dynamic Scaling of Growing Interfaces*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.889; Halpin-Healy and Takeuchi, 2015, *A KPZ Cocktail—Shaken, Not Stirred…*, arXiv:1505.01910.
solved_when: Exact critical exponents, distributions, or an equivalent solvable characterization of the strong-coupling KPZ universality class in two spatial dimensions are determined.
why: It would explain broad classes of nonequilibrium growth and fluctuating interfaces, where currently only numerical exponents are available in higher dimensions.
key_works: Kardar, Parisi, and Zhang, 1986, *Dynamic Scaling of Growing Interfaces*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.889; Halpin-Healy and Takeuchi, 2015, *A KPZ Cocktail—Shaken, Not Stirred…*, arXiv:1505.01910.

title: Gardner phase in finite-dimensional structural glasses
subfield: Soft matter, granular matter, and active materials
open: Does a sharp Gardner transition — the emergence of hierarchically organized marginal states — actually survive in realistic finite-dimensional structural glasses, or is it rounded into an avoided transition or smooth crossover by finite-dimensional fluctuations?
status: Mean-field theory predicts hierarchical marginal states, while simulations and experiments give suggestive but interpretation-dependent signatures. Key works: Charbonneau et al., 2014, *Fractal Free Energy Landscapes in Structural Glasses*; Berthier et al., 2019, *Gardner Physics in Amorphous Solids and Beyond*.
solved_when: A theory, simulation, or experiment establishes, by a controlled criterion, whether the Gardner transition in a finite-dimensional glass is genuinely sharp or a crossover; success means a definitive answer, with the finite-dimensional fate of the mean-field marginality hierarchy settled either way.
why: The answer determines how marginality governs glass stability and mechanical response, connecting the hierarchical organization of metastable states to measurable elastic and yielding behavior.
key_works: Charbonneau et al., 2014, *Fractal Free Energy Landscapes in Structural Glasses*; Berthier et al., 2019, *Gardner Physics in Amorphous Solids and Beyond*.

title: Three-dimensional Navier–Stokes regularity
open: Does every smooth initial velocity field for the incompressible three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations, under the Clay problem's conditions, remain smooth for all time — or can singularities form in finite time? Formally, one must prove global existence and smoothness, or construct a finite-time breakdown, for solutions emanating from smooth, divergence-free initial data.
status: Global weak solutions have been known since Leray (Jean Leray, 1934, *Sur le Mouvement d’un Liquide Visqueux Emplissant l’Espace*); smoothness and uniqueness in the required generality remain open. The Clay formulation is given in Charles Fefferman, 2000, *Existence and Smoothness of the Navier–Stokes Equation*.
solved_when: Either a proof of global-in-time smoothness is given under the Clay Millennium problem's stated conditions, or a finite-time singularity (breakdown) is constructed; the claim must satisfy the Clay Millennium Prize rules governing the award.
why: Resolves a foundational question about deterministic fluid evolution: whether the equations themselves constrain turbulence and singularity formation, or admit genuine breakdown.
key_works: Jean Leray, 1934, *Sur le Mouvement d’un Liquide Visqueux Emplissant l’Espace*; Charles Fefferman, 2000, *Existence and Smoothness of the Navier–Stokes Equation*.
prize: US$1 million Clay Millennium Prize, subject to its rules.
