title: Turbulent intermittency exponents
open: Can the anomalous scaling exponents and extreme-event statistics of three-dimensional turbulence be derived directly from the Navier–Stokes equations? A satisfactory solution would replace empirical multifractal fits with a first-principles computation of intermittency corrections.
status: Kolmogorov’s 1941 theory provides the baseline scaling, but the intermittency corrections remain incompletely understood; Uriel Frisch, 1995, *Turbulence: The Legacy of A. N. Kolmogorov*, DOI: 10.1017/CBO9781139170666, surveys the framework.
solved_when: The intermittency corrections to Kolmogorov’s baseline scaling — the anomalous exponents and the statistics of rare, intense events — are derived from the governing equations, with no appeal to empirical multifractal fitting.
why: It would give predictive power over rare, intense turbulent events that control mixing, structural loads, and reaction rates.
key_works: Uriel Frisch, 1995, *Turbulence: The Legacy of A. N. Kolmogorov*, DOI: 10.1017/CBO9781139170666.

title: Net-positive large-scale active drag reduction
open: Can active flow control be made to pay for itself at large scale? That is, can sustained drag reduction be demonstrated whose saved power substantially exceeds the combined actuation, sensing, and control costs under realistic fouling and changing flow conditions?
status: Large drag reductions have been achieved in selected laboratory conditions, but net energy benefit and robustness often diminish during scale-up. Key works: Quadrio, 2011, *Drag Reduction in Turbulent Boundary Layers by In-Plane Wall Motion*; Choi, Jeon, and Kim, 2008, *Control of Flow over a Bluff Body*.
solved_when: A demonstration shows sustained drag reduction at large scale in which saved power substantially exceeds actuation, sensing, and control costs, while robust to fouling and changing flow conditions.
why: Net-positive drag reduction would directly cut transportation and pumping energy; without net benefit and robustness, laboratory gains do not translate to real systems.
key_works: Quadrio, 2011, *Drag Reduction in Turbulent Boundary Layers by In-Plane Wall Motion*; Choi, Jeon, and Kim, 2008, *Control of Flow over a Bluff Body*.

title: Disruption avoidance at reactor conditions
open: Can a control system predict impending plasma disruptions at reactor conditions with enough warning and reliability to avoid them across operating scenarios? Formally, this means achieving sufficiently low missed-event and false-alarm rates across machines and regimes, with validated fallback mitigation when avoidance fails.
status: Machine-learning predictors and mitigation experiments have improved performance, but current systems must still be shown to generalize across machines and operating regimes. Key works: Hender et al., 2007, *Chapter 3: MHD Stability, Operational Limits and Disruptions*; de Vries et al., 2011, *Survey of Disruption Causes at JET*.
solved_when: A disruption-avoidance system demonstrates sufficiently low missed-event and false-alarm rates across operating scenarios and reactor conditions, together with validated fallback mitigation.
why: Unmitigated disruptions damage reactor structures; reliable avoidance protects those structures and supports high availability of a fusion plant.
key_works: Hender et al., 2007, *Chapter 3: MHD Stability, Operational Limits and Disruptions*; de Vries et al., 2011, *Survey of Disruption Causes at JET*.

title: Vacuum Schwinger pair production
open: Can we observe electron–positron pairs being created directly from the vacuum by an applied electromagnetic field, in a regime that cleanly identifies the nonperturbative Schwinger mechanism rather than some other pair-production channel?
status: The effect was predicted by Julian Schwinger in 1951 (*On Gauge Invariance and Vacuum Polarization*). Strong-field pair production through other mechanisms has been observed or explored, but these do not constitute the same observation; the Schwinger mechanism itself remains unobserved. Achieving it requires laser engineering beyond current practical intensity limits (see Di Piazza et al., 2012, *Extremely High-Intensity Laser Interactions with Fundamental Quantum Systems*, arXiv:1111.3886).
solved_when: A direct experimental observation of vacuum pair production attributable to the Schwinger mechanism is achieved, with a controlled field configuration that rules out competing mechanisms.
why: It would test a central nonperturbative prediction of quantum electrodynamics that has remained unconfirmed experimentally since its formulation.
key_works: Julian Schwinger, 1951, *On Gauge Invariance and Vacuum Polarization*; Di Piazza et al., 2012, *Extremely High-Intensity Laser Interactions with Fundamental Quantum Systems*, arXiv:1111.3886.

title: Laboratory optical vacuum birefringence
open: Can we measure the birefringence of the vacuum itself — a polarization-dependent refractive response of empty space induced by a controlled applied field — while rigorously excluding all material and instrumental birefringence?
status: Strong theoretical prediction and astrophysical indications exist, but they do not replace a clean laboratory optical measurement, which remains outstanding. Key works: Heisenberg and Euler, 1936, *Folgerungen aus der Diracschen Theorie des Positrons*; Di Piazza et al., 2012, arXiv:1111.3886.
solved_when: A laboratory optical measurement detects vacuum birefringence with applied controlled fields, at a sensitivity sufficient to distinguish the quantum-vacuum signal from material and instrumental birefringence backgrounds.
why: Such a measurement is a direct test of nonlinear vacuum electrodynamics as predicted by Heisenberg and Euler, moving beyond astrophysical indications to controlled laboratory confirmation.
key_works: Heisenberg and Euler, 1936, *Folgerungen aus der Diracschen Theorie des Positrons*; Di Piazza et al., 2012, arXiv:1111.3886.

title: Solid metallic hydrogen and its retained phases
subfield: Chemical physics, thermal physics, and extreme materials
open: Can solid hydrogen be made metallic in a reproducible way, and can any useful metallic phase survive after the pressure is released? More precisely, this asks for the crystal structures, electronic properties, and metastability of solid metallic hydrogen, including whether any phase persists at reduced pressure.
status: Conducting dense hydrogen has been reported and solid-state claims are debated, but the complete structural and metastability questions remain unsettled. Key works include Wigner and Huntington, 1935, *On the Possibility of a Metallic Modification of Hydrogen*; and McMahon et al., 2012, *The Properties of Hydrogen and Helium under Extreme Conditions*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.84.1607.
solved_when: The structures and electronic properties of solid metallic hydrogen are established with reproducible experimental confirmation, including a determination of whether any phase is retained after pressure reduction.
why: It probes the behavior of matter under extreme quantum conditions and could yield high-energy-density materials.
key_works: Wigner and Huntington, 1935, *On the Possibility of a Metallic Modification of Hydrogen*; McMahon et al., 2012, *The Properties of Hydrogen and Helium under Extreme Conditions*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.84.1607.

title: Predictive thermal boundary conductance
subfield: Chemical physics, thermal physics, and extreme materials
open: Can we predict the heat conductance of an interface from first principles — its atomic structure, bonding, disorder, and temperature — with a method that transfers across dissimilar material pairs? Formally, this asks for a theory or computational scheme whose accuracy is transferable rather than fitted to a given interface.
status: Acoustic and diffuse-mismatch models capture the limiting idealized cases, but real interfaces require the inclusion of anharmonic, electronic, and structural effects. Key works: Swartz and Pohl, 1989, *Thermal Boundary Resistance*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.61.605; Chen et al., 2022, *Interfacial Thermal Resistance: Past, Present, and Future*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.94.025002.
solved_when: A predictive scheme reproduces measured interface conductance across dissimilar materials from atomic structure, bonding, disorder, and temperature, without interface-specific fitting.
why: It removes a major bottleneck in electronics and thermal-management design, where interface resistance governs device heat dissipation.
key_works: Swartz and Pohl, 1989, *Thermal Boundary Resistance*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.61.605; Chen et al., 2022, *Interfacial Thermal Resistance: Past, Present, and Future*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.94.025002.

title: Microscopic identity of amorphous two-level systems
subfield: Chemical physics, thermal physics, and extreme materials
open: What, at the atomic level, are the two-level systems that universally govern the low-temperature properties of glasses, and can their density and coupling be predicted from first principles? A successful theory would identify the specific atomic structures and their tunneling dynamics in relevant amorphous materials and reproduce the observed density of states and coupling constants.
status: Phenomenological tunneling models date to the 1970s, notably Anderson, Halperin, and Varma, 1972, *Anomalous Low-Temperature Thermal Properties of Glasses and Spin Glasses* and Phillips, 1972, *Tunneling States in Amorphous Solids*; a universal microscopic account remains elusive.
solved_when: A microscopic account identifies the atomic structures and dynamics responsible for two-level-system behavior in relevant amorphous materials and correctly predicts their density and coupling.
why: It would show how to reduce loss and noise in superconducting circuits, resonators, and precision sensors, where these defects are the dominant limiting factor.
key_works: Anderson, Halperin, and Varma, 1972, *Anomalous Low-Temperature Thermal Properties of Glasses and Spin Glasses*; Phillips, 1972, *Tunneling States in Amorphous Solids*.

title: Functional significance of neural criticality
open: Does the scale-free activity observed in neural systems reflect genuine critical dynamics, and does operating near criticality causally improve computation or behavior rather than merely correlate with it?
status: Avalanche statistics motivate criticality models, but subsampling, nonstationarity, and alternative mechanisms can generate similar signatures. Key works: Beggs and Plenz, 2003, *Neuronal Avalanches in Neocortical Circuits*; Wilting and Priesemann, 2019, *25 Years of Criticality in Neuroscience—Established Results, Open Controversies, Novel Concepts*.
solved_when: A causal link is experimentally established (or ruled out) between a network's distance from criticality and its computational or behavioral performance, with controls for subsampling, nonstationarity, and alternative mechanisms that can produce avalanche-like statistics.
why: It tests whether criticality is a genuine organizing principle of brain dynamics rather than a statistical artifact, with direct implications for how network operating regimes support computation.
key_works: Beggs and Plenz, 2003, *Neuronal Avalanches in Neocortical Circuits*; Wilting and Priesemann, 2019, *25 Years of Criticality in Neuroscience—Established Results, Open Controversies, Novel Concepts*.

title: Lightning initiation
open: How does lightning actually get started? A complete theory must explain how leaders and electrical breakdown initiate under the conditions actually measured in thunderclouds, given that the observed large-scale fields fall well below simple conventional-breakdown thresholds.
status: Streamer, hydrometeor-enhancement, and runaway-electron mechanisms provide candidate ingredients; their respective roles remain debated. Key work: Dwyer and Uman, 2014, *The Physics of Lightning*, DOI: 10.1016/j.physrep.2013.09.004.
solved_when: A mechanism is established that quantitatively bridges measured thundercloud field strengths and hydrometeor conditions to leader initiation and breakdown, closing the gap with conventional-breakdown thresholds.
why: It explains a basic atmospheric electrical process and improves lightning protection models.
key_works: Dwyer and Uman, 2014, *The Physics of Lightning*, DOI: 10.1016/j.physrep.2013.09.004.

title: Collider-grade muon cooling
open: Can a muon beam be cooled in all six phase-space dimensions and delivered to collisions with the transmission and timing a high-energy muon collider requires, all before too many muons decay? Formally, this asks for an integrated cooling channel meeting collider-grade emittance, transmission, and bunch-timing specifications within the muon lifetime.
status: Ionization cooling itself has been experimentally demonstrated, but collider-grade integrated performance across all six dimensions is a much stronger requirement that remains unachieved. Key works: MICE Collaboration, 2020, *Demonstration of Cooling by the Muon Ionization Cooling Experiment*; International Muon Collider Collaboration, 2024, *Interim Report*, arXiv:2407.12450.
solved_when: An integrated six-dimensional ionization-cooling system is experimentally demonstrated to reach collider-grade emittance reduction, transmission, and timing — not merely channel-by-channel or single-mechanism performance — within the constraint of the muon lifetime.
why: Success would make compact lepton collisions at very high energies possible, something circular e⁺e⁻ machines cannot reach due to synchrotron-radiation losses.
key_works: MICE Collaboration, 2020, *Demonstration of Cooling by the Muon Ionization Cooling Experiment*; International Muon Collider Collaboration, 2024, *Interim Report*, arXiv:2407.12450.

title: Low-loss gravitational-wave mirror coatings
open: Can we produce optical coatings for gravitational-wave interferometer mirrors that combine low mechanical loss, low absorption, high reflectivity, and low scatter, while remaining manufacturable at the intended operating temperature and wavelength? Formally, the goal is a coating stack in which no one property is sacrificed to achieve the others.
status: Improving one coating property often degrades another, and coating thermal noise currently limits important detector bands (Harry et al., 2002, *Thermal Noise in Interferometric Gravitational Wave Detectors Due to Dielectric Optical Coatings*; Granata et al., 2020, *Amorphous Optical Coatings of Present Gravitational-Wave Interferometers*).
solved_when: A coating is demonstrated that simultaneously achieves low mechanical loss, low absorption, high reflectivity, low scatter, and manufacturability at the intended temperature and wavelength, as needed to reduce coating thermal noise in detector bands.
why: Such coatings would increase gravitational-wave observatory sensitivity without simply increasing laser power.
key_works: Harry et al., 2002, *Thermal Noise in Interferometric Gravitational Wave Detectors Due to Dielectric Optical Coatings*; Granata et al., 2020, *Amorphous Optical Coatings of Present Gravitational-Wave Interferometers*.

title: Newtonian-noise cancellation for ground-based observatories
open: Can we predict and subtract the gravity fluctuations produced by moving ground and air well enough to reach the intended low-frequency sensitivity of ground-based observatories, without subtracting genuine signals? Formally, can sensor-array measurements and site models reconstruct the local Newtonian gravitational field with the accuracy required for low-frequency noise cancellation?
status: Sensor-array methods and site models provide partial demonstrations; realistic environmental variability complicates full cancellation. Key works: Jan Harms, 2015, *Terrestrial Gravity Fluctuations*, arXiv:1507.05850.
solved_when: Newtonian-noise prediction and subtraction at a ground-based observatory achieves the intended low-frequency sensitivity while leaving genuine astrophysical signals intact, under realistic environmental variability.
why: Success opens lower-frequency gravitational-wave observations from Earth.
key_works: Jan Harms, 2015, *Terrestrial Gravity Fluctuations*, arXiv:1507.05850.

title: Cosmic coincidence problem
open: Why are the energy densities of dark energy and dark matter of the same order of magnitude in the Universe today, given that dark matter density diluted considerably over cosmic evolution and must have been far larger in the past? Is there some physical relation between the two energy densities that explains this near-equality now?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07); the energy densities of dark energy and dark matter are of the same order of magnitude, while dark matter energy density decreased during the universe's evolution and must have been very large in the past. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics
solved_when: A well-tested theoretical account explains the observed near-equality of the dark energy and dark matter energy densities at the present epoch, either deriving a relation between the two densities or showing why their coincidence at this epoch requires no fine-tuning.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Cosmological constant problem
open: Why does the zero-point energy of the vacuum not produce an enormous cosmological constant, and what mechanism cancels it out?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics); no solution is recorded.
solved_when: A theoretical framework is provided that explains, in quantitative agreement with the observed small cosmological constant, why the vacuum's zero-point energy does not gravitate as naively expected.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Shape of the universe
open: What is the global topology of a comoving spatial section of the universe — the 3-manifold informally called the "shape" of the universe? Neither curvature nor topology is currently known (curvature is known to be "close" to zero on observable scales), so the question remains whether the shape is unmeasurable, the Poincaré space, or some other 3-manifold.
solved_when: The topology (and curvature) of the comoving spatial section of the universe is determined — whether it is flat, spherical, or hyperbolic, and which 3-manifold it is — or it is shown to be unmeasurable in principle.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Magnetic monopole
open: Do particles carrying magnetic charge exist — either as relics of a hotter, higher-energy epoch of the early universe or, perhaps, surviving today? Paul Dirac showed that the existence of certain types of magnetic monopoles would explain the observed quantization of electric charge, giving the question a deep theoretical stake.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), in its list of unsolved problems in physics (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics).
solved_when: A magnetic monopole is experimentally detected, or a well-established theoretical framework demonstrably excludes (or accounts for the absence of) monopoles in our present universe; the record states no further quantitative targets.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Neutron lifetime puzzle
open: What is the true lifetime of the free neutron? Decades of measurements by two independent methods — "bottle" experiments that count surviving ultracold neutrons and "beam" experiments that count decay protons from a neutron flux — yield persistently different values, and the field still lacks consilience on which (if either) is correct.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in physics (accessed 2026-10-07): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics
solved_when: The bottle and beam experimental programs converge on a single, mutually consistent value for the neutron lifetime, or a verified explanation reconciles the discrepancy.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Generations of matter
open: Why does nature contain exactly three generations of quarks and leptons rather than some other number? More sharply, is there a first-principles theory of Yukawa couplings that predicts the observed mass spectrum of quarks and leptons across the generations?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics).
solved_when: A theoretical framework exists that explains both why there are exactly three generations and derives the specific masses of quarks and leptons in each generation from first principles, with the predictions matching the observed values.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Neutrino mass
open: What is the absolute mass of the neutrinos, and what is their fundamental nature? More precisely, are neutrinos Dirac or Majorana fermions, is the mass hierarchy normal or inverted, and does the CP-violating phase vanish?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: The absolute neutrino masses are measured, and the Dirac-vs-Majorana question, the normal-vs-inverted mass hierarchy, and whether the CP-violating phase equals 0 are all determined.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Anomalous magnetic dipole moment
open: Why does the experimentally measured value of the muon's anomalous magnetic dipole moment differ significantly from its theoretically predicted value? In formal terms, what is the origin of the discrepancy between the measured "muon g − 2" and the Standard Model prediction for that constant?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07). Key works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics
solved_when: The discrepancy between the experimental measurement and the theoretical prediction of the muon's anomalous magnetic dipole moment is explained — that is, a calculation or measurement resolves whether the difference is real, and if so, identifies its physical origin.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Koide formula
open: Why do the charged lepton masses satisfy the Koide relation so precisely? The quantity (m_e + m_μ + m_τ)/(√m_e + √m_μ + √m_τ)² equals, to within one standard deviation of observations, a simple value — and it is unknown how such a simple value arises, or why it is exactly the arithmetic average of the possible extreme values (equal masses, and 1 when one mass dominates).
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07); see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics.
solved_when: A theoretical derivation explains why the charged lepton masses yield this value to within one standard deviation of experimental measurements, including why it sits exactly midway between the extremes of equal masses and single-mass dominance.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Kuiper cliff
open: Why does the number of objects in the Solar System's Kuiper belt fall off rapidly and unexpectedly beyond a radius of 50 astronomical units?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07); see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics.
solved_when: A validated physical explanation accounts for the sharp drop-off in Kuiper belt object counts beyond 50 astronomical units, consistent with observational surveys.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Flyby anomaly
open: Why do satellites performing a gravity assist around a planet sometimes emerge with a total energy that differs, by a tiny amount, from the value predicted by standard gravitational theory? A satisfactory account would identify the physical mechanism responsible for these small, unexplained residuals in the spacecraft's post-flyby energy.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A physical explanation accounts for the observed minute energy discrepancies during planetary flybys, with predictions matching the measured satellite energies (and ideally forecasting the effect for future flybys).
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: The lithium problem
open: Why does the abundance of lithium-7 predicted by Big Bang nucleosynthesis exceed the amount actually observed in very old (population II) stars? A successful answer must reconcile the theoretical prediction with the observational measurements within a well-tested cosmological model.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07) (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics).
solved_when: A validated physical mechanism or correction to the prediction is found that brings the predicted primordial lithium-7 abundance into agreement with the abundance observed in very old stars.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Gauge block wringing
open: What physical mechanism allows gauge blocks — hardened steel blocks with extremely flat surfaces — to be "wrung" together so firmly that they bond without adhesive? A complete account should identify the dominant forces (e.g., molecular adhesion, air pressure, interlocking of surface films) and predict the observed wringing strength.
solved_when: A quantitative physical model explains which mechanism(s) cause wringing and accounts for the measured adhesion between gauge blocks.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Liquid crystal
open: Can the nematic-to-smectic-A phase transition in liquid crystals be characterized as a universal phase transition? That is, can its critical behavior be described by universal exponents and scaling laws independent of microscopic details?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07). A review of experimental developments at this transition is given by A. Yethiraj, "Recent Experimental Developments at the Nematic to Smectic-A Liquid Crystal Phase Transition", Thermotropic Liquid Crystals: Recent Advances, ed. A. Ramamoorthy, Springer 2007, chapter 8.
solved_when: A theoretical characterization of the nematic–smectic-A transition as a universal phase transition is established and consistent with experiment, with critical exponents that are either universal or classified into a small number of universality classes.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Metal whiskering
open: Why do some metallic surfaces spontaneously sprout fine metal whiskers? A predictive theory of whisker formation is lacking: although compressive mechanical stress is known to encourage growth, the underlying mechanism by which metal atoms assemble into these crystalline filaments has yet to be determined.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics). Compressive mechanical stress is known to encourage whisker formation, but the growth mechanism remains undetermined.
solved_when: A physically validated mechanism is identified that explains whisker initiation and growth on stressed metallic surfaces and predicts their formation — including the role of compressive stress — well enough to guide prevention in electrical devices.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: The injection problem
open: What mechanism gives astrophysical particles their initial ("injection") energies, high enough that Fermi acceleration can subsequently act on them? In formal terms: identify and characterize the physical process responsible for producing the suprathermal seed population on which Fermi acceleration builds.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics).
solved_when: A physical mechanism for the injection of particles above the threshold energy required for Fermi acceleration is identified and demonstrated, theoretically or observationally, to operate in the relevant astrophysical environments.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Langmuir's paradox
open: Why do low-pressure plasmas so often exhibit Maxwellian electron velocity distributions even though electron–electron collisions are far too infrequent to bring about thermalization? A satisfactory answer would identify the mechanism, or set of mechanisms, that replaces binary Coulomb collisions as the route to equilibrium in such plasmas.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in physics (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics, as of 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A physical mechanism is identified and validated — theoretically or experimentally — that quantitatively accounts for the observed Maxwellian electron velocity distributions in low-pressure plasmas under conditions where electron–electron collision rates are too low for conventional thermalization.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Neutron drip-line map
open: Where does nuclear existence end? The goal is to determine, experimentally and theoretically, the last bound neutron-rich isotope of each element across the nuclear chart, and to explain the resulting drip-line map with predictive many-body theory that properly couples to the continuum.
status: Light-element boundaries are much better mapped than heavy ones, and extrapolation becomes difficult near weak binding and changing shell structure. A global theoretical survey of the nuclear landscape is given in Erler et al., 2012, *The Limits of the Nuclear Landscape*, DOI: 10.1038/nature11188.
solved_when: The neutron drip line is mapped (or predictively determined with quantified uncertainties) across the nuclear chart, with the positions of the last bound isotopes reproduced by continuum-coupled many-body theory.
why: The drip line defines the fundamental limits of nuclear existence and constrains nucleosynthesis pathways, including the r-process production of heavy elements.
key_works: Erler et al., 2012, *The Limits of the Nuclear Landscape*, DOI: 10.1038/nature11188.

title: Nonlinear fate of extremal Kerr perturbations
open: What ultimately happens to a physically admissible perturbation of an exactly extremal rotating black hole when the full nonlinear Einstein dynamics are taken into account? In particular, does the horizon instability known at the linear level destroy extremality, or can it produce genuinely new singular behavior?
status: Linear horizon instabilities have been studied since Aretakis's work. Hintz's June 2026 preprint claims full subextremal Kerr stability, which does not settle the extremal problem. Key works: Stefanos Aretakis, 2011, *Stability and Instability of Extreme Reissner–Nordström Black Hole Spacetimes for Linear Scalar Perturbations I*; Peter Hintz, 2026, *Nonlinear Stability of Subextremal Kerr Black Holes*, arXiv:2606.28253.
solved_when: The nonlinear asymptotic fate of extremal Kerr under admissible perturbations is determined — specifically, whether extremality is destroyed by the horizon instability or new singular behavior emerges, with a rigorous characterization of the endpoint.
why: It resolves a boundary case where the standard black-hole stability arguments change qualitatively, so techniques proven away from extremality cannot simply be reused there.
key_works: Stefanos Aretakis, 2011, *Stability and Instability of Extreme Reissner–Nordström Black Hole Spacetimes for Linear Scalar Perturbations I*; Peter Hintz, 2026, *Nonlinear Stability of Subextremal Kerr Black Holes*, arXiv:2606.28253.

title: Hawking radiation from an astrophysical black hole
open: Can we detect Hawking radiation emitted by an actual astrophysical black hole? That is, observe radiation attributable to the Hawking process from a real gravitational black hole while excluding competing emission mechanisms.
status: The effect was predicted in 1974–1975, notably by Stephen Hawking, 1975, *Particle Creation by Black Holes*, DOI: 10.1007/BF02345020. Analogue-horizon experiments are valuable but do not constitute detection from an astrophysical black hole. A recent reference is Mann, 2026, *Black-hole Thermodynamics*.
solved_when: A detection of radiation attributable to the Hawking process from an astrophysical black hole is reported, with competing emission mechanisms ruled out.
why: It would directly test the meeting point of quantum fields, curved spacetime, and thermodynamics.
key_works: Stephen Hawking, 1975, *Particle Creation by Black Holes*, DOI: 10.1007/BF02345020; Mann, 2026, *Black-hole Thermodynamics*.

title: QCD axion discovery
open: Can we detect the QCD axion — the particle whose mass and couplings make it solve the strong-CP problem — as opposed to a generic axion-like particle? Formally, can an experimental search identify an axion whose mass and coupling constants lie in the region required by the Peccei–Quinn solution to strong CP?
status: The QCD axion was proposed in the 1970s. Haloscopes, helioscopes, and laboratory searches cover complementary but incomplete regions of the parameter space. Key works: Peccei and Quinn, 1977, *CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles*; David Marsh, 2016, *Axion Cosmology*, arXiv:1510.07633.
solved_when: An axion is detected with mass and couplings consistent with solving the strong-CP problem, and it is distinguished from a generic axion-like particle.
why: A discovery would simultaneously explain dark matter and the suppression of strong CP violation.
key_works: Peccei and Quinn, 1977, *CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles*; David Marsh, 2016, *Axion Cosmology*, arXiv:1510.07633.

title: Neutrino mass ordering
open: Is the third neutrino mass eigenstate heavier than the closely spaced solar pair (normal ordering), or lighter (inverted ordering)? Resolving this requires a determination robust against oscillation-parameter and detector uncertainties.
status: Global fits currently provide preferences rather than a universally decisive measurement. JUNO's first published 2026 oscillation results (JUNO Collaboration, 2026 first reactor-oscillation results, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-10538-z) improved solar-parameter measurements but did not themselves settle the ordering.
solved_when: A measurement (or global combination) establishes the mass ordering at a statistically decisive level, with systematic and oscillation uncertainties treated robustly, replacing current fit preferences with a settled result.
why: The ordering changes how neutrinoless double-beta decay results are interpreted and constrains models of neutrino flavor.
key_works: JUNO Collaboration, 2026 first reactor-oscillation results, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-10538-z.

title: Atmospheric mixing-angle octant
open: Is the atmospheric mixing angle below, above, or exactly at maximal mixing? Formally, this asks for a determination of the octant of θ23 that resolves its degeneracies with the other oscillation parameters.
status: Precision has improved substantially since atmospheric oscillations were established, but octant determination remains a distinct task from proving oscillations or measuring a mass splitting. Key work: de Gouvêa et al., 2022, arXiv:2209.07983.
solved_when: The octant of θ23 (lower, upper, or exactly maximal mixing) is determined in a way that resolves the degeneracies with other oscillation parameters.
why: The answer discriminates among flavor-symmetry models of neutrino mixing.
key_works: de Gouvêa et al., 2022, arXiv:2209.07983.

title: Net-electric fusion power
open: Can a fusion system be operated so that it exports sustained net electricity to the grid, once every plant-level load — drivers, magnets, cryogenics, fuel processing, cooling, and maintenance — is accounted for?
status: Plasma gain and target gain are not net-electric gain, and integrated electricity production remains a stronger engineering target than any gain metric achieved so far. A relevant framing appears in National Academies, 2021, *Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid*, DOI: 10.17226/25991.
solved_when: A fusion system demonstrates sustained net-electric output after subtracting all recirculating power and plant overheads; plasma gain or target gain alone does not qualify.
why: This turns fusion from a plasma milestone into a deliverable energy technology; without net electricity, fusion remains a physics demonstration rather than a power source.
key_works: National Academies, 2021, *Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid*, DOI: 10.17226/25991.

title: Reproducible ambient-pressure room-temperature superconductivity
open: Can a material be made that superconducts at ordinary room temperature and ambient pressure, with the result independently replicated through resistance, magnetic, and thermodynamic evidence? In formal terms, is there a reproducible compound whose superconducting transition occurs near room temperature at ambient pressure?
status: High-pressure hydrides demonstrate very high transition temperatures, while controversial ambient-pressure claims do not satisfy the required evidence standard. Key works: Drozdov et al., 2019, *Superconductivity at 250 K in Lanthanum Hydride under High Pressures*, arXiv:1812.01567; Pickett, 2023, *Colloquium: Room Temperature Superconductivity: The Roles of Theory and Materials Design at High Pressure*.
solved_when: A material is produced that superconducts near room temperature at ambient pressure, and the finding is independently replicated through resistance, magnetic, and thermodynamic evidence.
why: It could transform electrical systems, magnets, and sensing, subject to current-density and manufacturability constraints.
key_works: Drozdov et al., 2019, *Superconductivity at 250 K in Lanthanum Hydride under High Pressures*, arXiv:1812.01567; Pickett, 2023, *Colloquium: Room Temperature Superconductivity: The Roles of Theory and Materials Design at High Pressure*.

title: Yang–Mills theory
open: Given an arbitrary compact gauge group, does a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory with a finite mass gap exist?
solved_when: A rigorous construction of a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory is provided for an arbitrary compact gauge group, together with a proof that it exhibits a finite mass gap. This problem is one of the Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Quantum field theory
open: Can a genuinely interacting quantum field theory in four-dimensional spacetime be constructed with full mathematical rigor, without recourse to perturbative methods? Formally, this asks for an existence construction satisfying the Wightman-style axioms (or an equivalent rigorous framework) for an interacting QFT in 4 dimensions.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07 (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics).
solved_when: A mathematically rigorous construction of an interacting, non-perturbative quantum field theory in four-dimensional spacetime is given, meeting accepted axiomatic standards for QFT.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Dark matter
open: What is dark matter made of? More formally, is it a particle — a weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP), an axion, the lightest superpartner (LSP), or something else — or are the phenomena attributed to dark matter instead the result of a modified theory of gravity distinct from general relativity?
status: Despite extensive research, the exact composition of dark matter remains unknown; the problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07.
solved_when: The exact composition of dark matter is identified, or an alternate theory of gravity is established that accounts for the phenomena currently attributed to it.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Galaxy rotation problem
open: Is dark matter responsible for the gap between observed stellar orbital speeds in galaxies and the speeds predicted by standard gravitational theory, or is some other explanation needed?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics).
solved_when: A validated account of the discrepancy between predicted and observed galaxy rotation curves is established — either through direct detection of dark matter consistent with observed rotation curves, or through a demonstrated alternative that reproduces them.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Topological order
open: Can topological order survive at non-zero temperature, or does thermal noise inevitably destroy it? Equally, can a three-dimensional stabilizer code realize a self-correcting quantum memory that needs no active error correction to preserve qubits?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in physics (checked 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof or construction is given that topological order is (or is not) stable at non-zero temperature — equivalently, that a three-dimensional self-correcting quantum memory in the stabilizer-code framework does (or does not) exist.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Four-dimensional Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
open: Can one construct a genuine quantum Yang–Mills theory on four-dimensional spacetime for every compact simple gauge group, satisfying appropriate axioms of a quantum field theory, and prove that it has a strictly positive mass gap?
status: The Clay formulation dates to 2000, though the underlying difficulty goes back to the development of non-Abelian gauge theory. Lattice calculations provide compelling physical evidence but not the required continuum construction. Key work: Arthur Jaffe and Edward Witten, 2000, *Quantum Yang–Mills Theory*, official Clay problem description.
solved_when: A mathematically rigorous construction exists of a nontrivial quantum Yang–Mills theory on four-dimensional spacetime for every compact simple gauge group, satisfying the appropriate axioms, together with a proof of a strictly positive mass gap, under the rules of the US$1 million Clay Millennium Prize.
why: It would place a mathematically rigorous foundation under an essential part of the Standard Model, where the mass gap underlies phenomena such as confinement.
key_works: Arthur Jaffe and Edward Witten, 2000, *Quantum Yang–Mills Theory*, official Clay problem description.
prize: US$1 million Clay Millennium Prize, subject to its rules.

title: Nonperturbative construction of general chiral gauge theories
open: Can general anomaly-free chiral gauge theories — including the full fermion content of the Standard Model — be constructed nonperturbatively with a regulator that is local, gauge-invariant, and yields a well-defined continuum limit? In other words, is there a lattice or otherwise nonperturbative construction that avoids fermion doubling and preserves the chiral gauge structure without recourse to perturbation theory?
status: The obstruction has been central since lattice fermion doubling was understood. Ginsparg–Wilson, overlap, and domain-wall methods solve important components of the problem, but a universally satisfactory construction remains more difficult than for vectorlike QCD. Key works include Ginsparg and Wilson, 1982, *A Remnant of Chiral Symmetry on the Lattice*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevD.25.2649, and Davoudi et al., 2022, arXiv:2209.10758.
solved_when: A local, gauge-invariant regulator and continuum construction exists for general anomaly-free chiral gauge theories, covering the complete Standard Model fermion content.
why: It would enable genuinely nonperturbative calculations in chiral particle theories, which are currently out of reach beyond perturbative methods.
key_works: Ginsparg and Wilson, 1982, *A Remnant of Chiral Symmetry on the Lattice*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevD.25.2649; Davoudi et al., 2022, arXiv:2209.10758.

title: Intrinsic construction of the six-dimensional (2,0) theory
open: Can the interacting six-dimensional (2,0) theories be given an intrinsic definition, with computable local observables and a controlled nonperturbative prescription, that does not rely on an auxiliary string-theory embedding?
status: The theories were identified in the 1990s through string/M-theory. Compactifications, protected sectors, and dualities reveal substantial structure without yielding an ordinary complete formulation. Key works: Edward Witten, 1995, *Some Comments on String Dynamics*, hep-th/9507121; Poland and Rastelli, 2022, *Snowmass Topical Summary: Formal QFT*, arXiv:2210.03128.
solved_when: A definition of the interacting six-dimensional (2,0) theories exists that is intrinsic (no string/M-theory embedding required), yields computable local observables, and supplies a controlled nonperturbative prescription.
why: Such a construction would organize dualities and strongly coupled theories across multiple dimensions, turning a currently structure-revealing but incomplete subject into a working framework.
key_works: Edward Witten, 1995, *Some Comments on String Dynamics*, hep-th/9507121; Poland and Rastelli, 2022, *Snowmass Topical Summary: Formal QFT*, arXiv:2210.03128.

title: Resurgent completion of four-dimensional gauge theory
open: Can a physically important four-dimensional gauge theory be given a controlled transseries representation that unifies its perturbative, instanton, and renormalon sectors into unambiguous observables? In other words, can resurgent methods be extended from quantum mechanics to ordinary four-dimensional confining gauge theories with full control?
status: Resurgence works impressively in quantum mechanics and selected lower-dimensional or compactified theories, but extending comparable control to ordinary four-dimensional confining theories remains unresolved. Key works: Daniele Dorigoni, 2014, *An Introduction to Resurgence, Trans-Series and Alien Calculus*, arXiv:1411.3585; Poland and Rastelli, 2022, arXiv:2210.03128.
solved_when: A controlled transseries is constructed for a physically important four-dimensional gauge theory, incorporating the perturbative, instanton, and renormalon sectors and yielding unambiguous observables.
why: It would turn divergent perturbation theory into a systematic nonperturbative computational method.
key_works: Daniele Dorigoni, 2014, *An Introduction to Resurgence, Trans-Series and Alien Calculus*, arXiv:1411.3585; Poland and Rastelli, 2022, arXiv:2210.03128.

title: All-loop color–kinematics duality
open: Under what precise general conditions do gauge-theory scattering amplitudes admit numerator factors obeying the same algebraic identities as their color factors, at arbitrary loop order? A sharper formal version asks for a characterization, constructive or obstructive, of when color–kinematics duality holds at all multiplicities and loop orders.
status: Since 2008, many explicit constructions and important tree-level results have accumulated (Bern, Carrasco, and Johansson, 2008, *New Relations for Gauge-Theory Amplitudes*, arXiv:0805.3993). A universal loop-level construction or definitive obstruction classification remains unavailable.
solved_when: A universal construction of loop-level numerators satisfying color–kinematics duality at arbitrary loop order is established, or a definitive classification of obstructions is given.
why: It would systematize the double-copy computation of gravitational scattering amplitudes, turning quantum-gravity calculations into an algebraic procedure inherited from gauge theory.
key_works: Bern, Carrasco, and Johansson, 2008, *New Relations for Gauge-Theory Amplitudes*, arXiv:0805.3993; Poland and Rastelli, 2022, arXiv:2210.03128.

title: Complete unitary black-hole evaporation
open: Can a black hole that forms from collapse in asymptotically flat spacetime evaporate in a way that is fully compatible with unitary quantum evolution? A complete answer should give a unitary description of the entire formation-and-evaporation process, including operationally accessible outgoing observables and the fate of information that fell in.
status: The information problem dates to the 1970s. Holography, islands, and replica calculations reproduce important entropy behavior but do not supply every ingredient of a realistic evaporation process. Key works: Stephen Hawking, 1976, *Breakdown of Predictability in Gravitational Collapse*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevD.14.2460; Geoff Penington, 2019, *Entanglement Wedge Reconstruction and the Information Paradox*, arXiv:1905.08255.
solved_when: A derivation exists of a complete, unitary description of formation and evaporation of an asymptotically flat black hole, covering both the operationally accessible outgoing observables and the fate of infalling information.
why: It reconciles quantum mechanics with gravitational collapse, determining whether predictability is truly lost when black holes form and evaporate.
key_works: Stephen Hawking, 1976, *Breakdown of Predictability in Gravitational Collapse*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevD.14.2460; Geoff Penington, 2019, *Entanglement Wedge Reconstruction and the Information Paradox*, arXiv:1905.08255.

title: Microstates of generic astrophysical black holes
open: Can we identify and count the microscopic quantum states of a generic astrophysical black hole — an ordinary rotating, nonextremal Kerr hole — well enough to reproduce its entropy from first principles? More formally, can a state count be given for generic nonextremal rotating black holes that yields the entropy together with controlled corrections, without relying on supersymmetry?
status: Since the Strominger–Vafa result of 1996 (Strominger and Vafa, *Microscopic Origin of the Bekenstein–Hawking Entropy*, hep-th/9601029), controlled microscopic counting has been achieved only for special, largely supersymmetric black holes; generic astrophysical Kerr black holes remain substantially harder. A recent overview is Robert Mann, 2026, *Black-hole Thermodynamics*, DOI: 10.1038/s42254-026-00942-9.
solved_when: A microscopic state counting for generic nonextremal rotating (astrophysical Kerr) black holes is exhibited that reproduces the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy and its corrections in a controlled approximation, with no appeal to supersymmetry.
why: It would explain black-hole entropy as an actual enumeration of states rather than a thermodynamic analogy, closing the gap between string-theoretic counting and the black holes actually observed in the sky.
key_works: Strominger and Vafa, 1996, *Microscopic Origin of the Bekenstein–Hawking Entropy*, hep-th/9601029; Robert Mann, 2026, *Black-hole Thermodynamics*, DOI: 10.1038/s42254-026-00942-9.

title: State-independent black-hole interior reconstruction
open: Can the black-hole interior be described by operators reconstructed from exterior quantum data in a way that does not depend on which black-hole state is chosen, and if so, how large a family of states can such state-independent operators cover? More precisely, the problem is to determine the domain of validity — and the limitations — of reconstructing interior observables from exterior data, including whether state-independent operators can describe sufficiently large families of black-hole states.
status: The problem was sharpened during the 2010s by holographic quantum error correction and firewall arguments. Existing reconstructions involve code subspaces, restricted observables, or state-dependence questions. Key works: Penington, 2019, arXiv:1905.08255; Almheiri, Marolf, Polchinski, and Sully, 2013, *Black Holes: Complementarity or Firewalls?*, arXiv:1207.3123.
solved_when: A precise characterization exists of which interior observables are reconstructible from exterior quantum data and for which families of black-hole states, together with a determination of whether state-independent reconstructions are possible for sufficiently large state families or a proof that state-dependence is unavoidable.
why: It clarifies what locality and an interior mean in quantum gravity, directly bearing on whether complementarity or firewalls follow from the holographic description.
key_works: Penington, 2019, arXiv:1905.08255; Almheiri, Marolf, Polchinski, and Sully, 2013, *Black Holes: Complementarity or Firewalls?*, arXiv:1207.3123.

title: Controlled de Sitter vacua in string theory
open: Do fully controlled, metastable de Sitter solutions exist in string theory? The task is to construct such vacua with all relevant moduli, quantum corrections, and localized-source effects accounted for, or to prove impossibility under well-defined assumptions.
status: The KKLT proposal dates to 2003 (Kachru, Kallosh, Linde, and Trivedi, 2003, *de Sitter Vacua in String Theory*, hep-th/0301240). Numerous constructions, consistency checks, criticisms, and no-go results apply to different regimes; a universal settlement is absent. Related swampland constraints are surveyed in Harlow et al., 2023, *Weak Gravity Conjecture*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.035003.
solved_when: Either a metastable de Sitter vacuum is exhibited with complete control over moduli stabilization, quantum corrections, and localized sources, or a no-go theorem is established under clearly stated assumptions that rules out such vacua.
why: It tests whether the leading ultraviolet-completion frameworks of quantum gravity can accommodate the observed cosmic acceleration, and its resolution either anchors string phenomenology in cosmology or forces a revision of how these frameworks connect to our universe.
key_works: Kachru, Kallosh, Linde, and Trivedi, 2003, *de Sitter Vacua in String Theory*, hep-th/0301240; Harlow et al., 2023, *Weak Gravity Conjecture*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.035003.

title: Physical resolution of spacetime singularities
open: Derive nonsingular, predictive evolution through black-hole or cosmological singularities in a theory that also reproduces tested low-energy gravity.
status: Classical singularity theorems date to the 1960s. Quantum-cosmology bounces and other mechanisms work in selected models — e.g. Ashtekar, Pawlowski, and Singh, 2006, *Quantum Nature of the Big Bang*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.141301, and Strominger, 2009, arXiv:0906.1313 — but their generality and observational meaning remain unsettled.
solved_when: A single framework is shown both to reproduce tested low-energy gravity and to yield deterministic, nonsingular evolution through black-hole and cosmological singularities, with the mechanism's generality and observational consequences established.
why: It determines whether the laws of physics remain predictive at gravitational extremes; without it, physics admits regimes where evolution simply breaks down.
key_works: Ashtekar, Pawlowski, and Singh, 2006, *Quantum Nature of the Big Bang*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.141301; Strominger, 2009, arXiv:0906.1313.

title: Weak Gravity Conjecture
open: Does every consistent theory of quantum gravity require charged states that are light enough relative to their charge to be superextremal? More precisely, can precise versions of this Weak Gravity Conjecture be proved or disproved, and which formulations survive when extended to multiple gauge fields, scalar couplings, and higher-form fields?
status: Introduced in 2006. String examples and black-hole arguments support several forms of the conjecture, but different formulations have different evidence and counterexamples. Key works: Arkani-Hamed et al., 2007, *The String Landscape, Black Holes and Gravity as the Weakest Force*, hep-th/0601001; Harlow et al., 2023, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.035003.
solved_when: A rigorous proof or disproof of a precise formulation of the conjecture is established, including a determination of which versions hold in the presence of multiple gauge fields, scalar couplings, and higher-form fields.
why: It could serve as a criterion separating low-energy theories that can coexist with quantum gravity from those that cannot, constraining the space of consistent theories.
key_works: Arkani-Hamed et al., 2007, *The String Landscape, Black Holes and Gravity as the Weakest Force*, hep-th/0601001; Harlow et al., 2023, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.035003.

title: The problem of time in quantum gravity
open: Can quantum gravity be formulated so that dynamics is well-defined even when spacetime itself is quantum and no global time variable exists? In other words, construct a framework in which physical clocks, relational evolution, and observable probabilities emerge consistently from the gravitational constraints, including situations without a globally useful time variable.
status: The problem has been present since canonical quantum gravity in the 1960s. Relational clocks and deparametrized models resolve restricted cases, but not all clock choices and quantum geometries. Key works: Bryce DeWitt, 1967, *Quantum Theory of Gravity. I. The Canonical Theory*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRev.160.1113; Chris Isham, 1992, *Canonical Quantum Gravity and the Problem of Time*, gr-qc/9210011.
solved_when: A single consistent formulation is constructed in which physical clocks, relational evolution, and observable probabilities all follow from the gravitational constraints, covering arbitrary clock choices and general quantum geometries — not merely restricted, deparametrized cases.
why: It gives operational meaning to dynamics when spacetime itself is quantum; without it, predictions in quantum gravity lack a well-defined notion of evolution.
key_works: Bryce DeWitt, 1967, *Quantum Theory of Gravity. I. The Canonical Theory*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRev.160.1113; Chris Isham, 1992, *Canonical Quantum Gravity and the Problem of Time*, gr-qc/9210011.

title: Weak cosmic censorship
open: Can singularities arising from gravitational collapse ever be visible to distant observers, or are they always hidden behind horizons? Formally: do there exist generic, physically admissible asymptotically flat initial data that produce singularities visible from infinity — with a specified matter model and a precise meaning of "generic"?
status: Proposed by Penrose in 1969. Symmetric models, numerical examples, and conditional theorems establish substantial but incomplete territory. Key works include Roger Penrose, 1969, *Gravitational Collapse: The Role of General Relativity*, and Demetrios Christodoulou, 1999, *The Instability of Naked Singularities in the Gravitational Collapse of a Scalar Field*.
solved_when: A rigorous theorem settles, for a specified matter model and a specified notion of generic initial data, whether naked singularities (singularities visible from infinity) can or cannot form from such data.
why: It determines whether external observers can lose predictive access to spacetime evolution: if censorship fails, physics as seen from infinity ceases to be well-determined.
key_works: Roger Penrose, 1969, *Gravitational Collapse: The Role of General Relativity*; Demetrios Christodoulou, 1999, *The Instability of Naked Singularities in the Gravitational Collapse of a Scalar Field*.

title: Cosmological constant naturalness
open: Why is the vacuum-energy density of our universe so extraordinarily small, and can this smallness be explained in a framework that is stable under radiative corrections while still reproducing known particle physics and cosmology?
status: The modern naturalness problem has been explicit for decades, notably framed in Steven Weinberg, 1989, *The Cosmological Constant Problem*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1, and reviewed more recently in Green et al., 2022, *Snowmass Theory Frontier: Astrophysics and Cosmology*, arXiv:2209.06854. Renormalization allows fitting the measured value but does not explain its smallness or radiative stability; no accepted solution exists.
solved_when: A radiatively stable mechanism is provided that explains the observed small vacuum-energy density and is consistent with established particle physics and cosmological observations.
why: It addresses a central mismatch between quantum-field-theoretic expectations for vacuum energy and what gravity observes; renormalization can fit the measured value but leaves its smallness and stability unexplained.
key_works: Steven Weinberg, 1989, *The Cosmological Constant Problem*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1; Green et al., 2022, *Snowmass Theory Frontier: Astrophysics and Cosmology*, arXiv:2209.06854.

title: Hubble-constant inference discrepancy
open: Can the disagreement between early-universe and late-universe measurements of the expansion rate be brought into agreement? A satisfactory resolution would identify the systematics responsible, revise the astrophysical calibration, or provide a model that consistently fits all relevant data.
status: The discrepancy sharpened during the 2010s. Its significance depends on the datasets and modeling used; simply proposing an early-dark-energy component is not a solution. Key works: Verde, Treu, and Riess, 2019, *Tensions between the Early and Late Universe*, arXiv:1907.10625; Green et al., 2022, arXiv:2209.06854.
solved_when: Early-universe and late-universe determinations of the Hubble constant agree within their uncertainties once identified systematics, revised calibrations, or a consistent model are applied, with no residual significance dependent on dataset or modeling choices.
why: A resolution could reveal new cosmological physics, or expose important limitations in how precision inference is done.
key_works: Verde, Treu, and Riess, 2019, *Tensions between the Early and Late Universe*, arXiv:1907.10625; Green et al., 2022, arXiv:2209.06854.

title: Microphysical identity of inflation
open: What fields, interactions, and initial conditions drove the primordial accelerated expansion of the universe? Alternatively, is there a distinguishable non-inflationary mechanism that produces the observed primordial perturbations?
status: Inflationary models date to the early 1980s. Observations constrain broad classes of models but do not identify a unique microscopic mechanism. Key works: Alan Guth, 1981, *Inflationary Universe: A Possible Solution to the Horizon and Flatness Problems*; Daniel Baumann, 2009, *TASI Lectures on Inflation*, arXiv:0907.5424.
solved_when: The microscopic degrees of freedom and dynamics responsible for inflation are identified, or a distinguishable alternative mechanism is established that reproduces the observed primordial perturbations.
why: A solution would tie the universe's initial conditions directly to fundamental physics, turning a phenomenological stage of cosmic history into a testable microphysical theory.
key_works: Alan Guth, 1981, *Inflationary Universe: A Possible Solution to the Horizon and Flatness Problems*; Daniel Baumann, 2009, *TASI Lectures on Inflation*, arXiv:0907.5424.

title: Reheating history
open: How did the universe, emerging from inflation or some alternative primordial state, convert its stored energy into particles and reach a hot thermal bath? More precisely, what were the reheating temperature, the equation-of-state history, and the route by which equilibrium was approached?
status: Perturbative decay, preheating, and lattice simulations describe candidate mechanisms; see Amin, Hertzberg, Kaiser, and Karouby, 2014, *Nonperturbative Dynamics of Reheating after Inflation: A Review*, arXiv:1410.3808. Observations have not yet selected the actual thermalization history.
solved_when: A concrete thermalization history is determined — specifying the reheating temperature, the equation-of-state evolution, and the approach to equilibrium — and shown to be consistent with observation, thereby selecting among candidate mechanisms.
why: It is the bridge between primordial cosmology and the observed world: the answer constrains dark matter production, baryogenesis, and relic abundances.
key_works: Amin, Hertzberg, Kaiser, and Karouby, 2014, *Nonperturbative Dynamics of Reheating after Inflation: A Review*, arXiv:1410.3808.

title: Origin of the baryon asymmetry
open: What mechanism generated the tiny excess of matter over antimatter that survived the early universe, and can it be experimentally pinned down? Formally, the goal is to identify a dynamical scenario satisfying Sakharov's conditions that quantitatively produces the observed cosmic baryon asymmetry and yields testable, experimentally constrainable predictions.
status: Sakharov's conditions for baryogenesis date to 1967. Electroweak baryogenesis, leptogenesis, and other scenarios remain viable candidates; however, reproducing the observed asymmetry through parameter choice does not amount to identification of the mechanism.
solved_when: A specific mechanism is identified whose quantitative output matches the observed baryon asymmetry and which is experimentally constrained — that is, subject to observational or experimental tests that can confirm or rule it out, rather than merely reproducing the asymmetry by parameter choice.
why: It explains why ordinary matter survived annihilation in the observable universe rather than leaving a cosmos of pure radiation.
key_works: Andrei Sakharov, 1967, *Violation of CP Invariance, C Asymmetry, and Baryon Asymmetry of the Universe*; Morrissey and Ramsey-Musolf, 2012, *Electroweak Baryogenesis*, arXiv:1206.2942.

title: Origin of intergalactic magnetic fields
open: Are the magnetic fields pervading intergalactic space primordial, dating from the early universe, or were they seeded later by astrophysical processes — and can we reconstruct how they were produced and amplified over cosmic history?
status: Multiple magnetogenesis mechanisms have been proposed, but observational inferences and upper/lower bounds on intergalactic magnetic fields remain model-dependent. A reference for the field is Durrer and Neronov, 2013, *Cosmological Magnetic Fields: Their Generation, Evolution and Observation*, arXiv:1303.7121.
solved_when: A determination of whether intergalactic seed fields are primordial or astrophysically generated is established, together with a reconstruction of their production and amplification history, in a way that is no longer model-dependent.
why: Settling the origin of these fields would open a new probe of early-universe processes and structure formation.
key_works: Durrer and Neronov, 2013, *Cosmological Magnetic Fields: Their Generation, Evolution and Observation*, arXiv:1303.7121.

title: Sub-GeV dark matter at material excitation thresholds
open: Can specified sub-GeV dark matter models be detected — or robustly excluded — via electron, phonon, magnon, or other low-energy material excitations? Success requires sensitivity at the relevant excitation thresholds together with calibrated backgrounds in that regime.
status: Semiconductor, superconducting, and collective-excitation detectors have opened new sensitivity regions, but unexplained low-energy excesses and material-response uncertainties remain limiting. Key works: Boveia et al., 2022, arXiv:2211.07027; Barbeau et al., 2022, *Report of the Instrumentation Frontier Working Group for Snowmass 2021*.
solved_when: A detection is reported, or a robust exclusion of the specified light-dark-matter models is established, using electron, phonon, magnon, or other low-energy excitations with backgrounds calibrated at the relevant thresholds.
why: It tests dark matter candidates inaccessible to conventional nuclear-recoil searches, which lose sensitivity at sub-GeV masses.
key_works: Boveia et al., 2022, arXiv:2211.07027; Barbeau et al., 2022, *Report of the Instrumentation Frontier Working Group for Snowmass 2021*.

title: Dark-matter self-interactions versus baryonic feedback
open: Do the observed halo cores, the diversity of small-scale structure, and related small-scale anomalies demand new dark-matter self-interactions, or can baryonic feedback alone account for them within the standard collisionless cold-dark-matter picture?
status: Simulations reproduce selected observations through different mechanisms, and their degeneracy prevents a unique interpretation. See Bullock and Boylan-Kolchin, 2017, *Small-Scale Challenges to the ΛCDM Paradigm*, arXiv:1707.04256.
solved_when: A quantitative analysis shows either that baryonic processes within collisionless ΛCDM reproduce the full set of small-scale observations (cores, diversity, and related anomalies), or that no viable baryonic feedback model can do so, thereby isolating dark-matter self-interactions as the required explanation.
why: A resolution would either vindicate collisionless dark matter or reveal new dark-sector forces acting on galactic scales.
key_works: Bullock and Boylan-Kolchin, 2017, *Small-Scale Challenges to the ΛCDM Paradigm*, arXiv:1707.04256.

title: Ultralight dark-matter wave signatures
open: Can we identify — or rule out — coherent wave effects of ultralight dark matter by combining structure, timing, lensing, and laboratory measurements into a single mutually consistent picture?
status: Wave-supported cores and interference patterns are calculable; translating observations into robust mass bounds requires handling baryonic and astrophysical uncertainties. Key works: Hu, Barkana, and Gruzinov, 2000, *Fuzzy Cold Dark Matter: The Wave Properties of Ultralight Particles*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.1158; Marsh, 2016, arXiv:1510.07633.
solved_when: A combined analysis of structural, timing, lensing, and laboratory observations either detects a coherent wave signature of ultralight dark matter or excludes it, with baryonic and astrophysical uncertainties robustly controlled.
why: It tests matter whose astronomical behavior is explicitly quantum mechanical, probing dark matter as waves rather than particles.
key_works: Hu, Barkana, and Gruzinov, 2000, *Fuzzy Cold Dark Matter: The Wave Properties of Ultralight Particles*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.1158; Marsh, 2016, arXiv:1510.07633.

title: Primordial-black-hole dark-matter fraction
open: Do primordial black holes make up an appreciable fraction of the dark matter in any mass distribution still allowed by observation, including extended rather than monochromatic populations?
status: Lensing, evaporation, accretion, and gravitational-wave observations each constrain different mass windows. A 2026 subsolar-binary search (Kacanja et al., 2026, *Search for Sub-Solar Mass Binaries in the First Part of LIGO’s Fourth Observing Run*, arXiv:2602.12115) reported no detection, tightening constraints rather than eliminating every scenario; broader constraints are compiled in Carr et al., 2021, *Constraints on Primordial Black Holes*, arXiv:2002.12778.
solved_when: The dark-matter fraction attributable to primordial black holes is determined (or meaningfully bounded) across all allowed mass windows, extended as well as monochromatic, combining lensing, evaporation, accretion, and gravitational-wave constraints.
why: A determination would simultaneously test the nature of dark matter and the spectrum of primordial density fluctuations in the early universe.
key_works: Carr et al., 2021, *Constraints on Primordial Black Holes*, arXiv:2002.12778; Kacanja et al., 2026, *Search for Sub-Solar Mass Binaries in the First Part of LIGO’s Fourth Observing Run*, arXiv:2602.12115.

title: Dark-matter discrimination inside the neutrino fog
open: How can a direct-detection experiment tell a dark-matter signal apart from the neutrino background once both produce indistinguishable recoils? The goal is a scalable discrimination method — exploiting direction, timing, multiple target materials, or other observables — that separates a specified dark-matter signal from neutrino-induced recoils.
status: The neutrino background is understood not to be an absolute impossibility floor, and the open challenge is obtaining enough discriminating information at realistic exposures and thresholds. Key work: Billard, Strigari, and Figueroa-Feliciano, 2014, *Implication of Neutrino Backgrounds on the Reach of Next Generation Dark Matter Direct Detection Experiments*, arXiv:1307.5458.
solved_when: A method is demonstrated that, at realistic exposures and detection thresholds, extracts enough discriminating information to distinguish a specified dark-matter signal from the neutrino background; since the record states no quantitative targets, this is the natural criterion.
why: It preserves the discovery potential of dark-matter searches as detectors become sensitive enough that neutrinos mimic the signal; without it, the neutrino background becomes an effective wall for direct detection.
key_works: Billard, Strigari, and Figueroa-Feliciano, 2014, *Implication of Neutrino Backgrounds on the Reach of Next Generation Dark Matter Direct Detection Experiments*, arXiv:1307.5458.

title: Electroweak hierarchy mechanism
open: Why is the Higgs mass so far below plausible ultraviolet scales rather than the result of unexplained parameter tuning? Identify a predictive mechanism for this hierarchy that yields observable consequences distinguishing it from fine-tuning.
status: Naturalness motivated supersymmetry, compositeness, and other proposals for decades, but no experimentally established mechanism has emerged. Foundational framing traces to Gerard ’t Hooft, 1980, *Naturalness, Chiral Symmetry, and Spontaneous Chiral Symmetry Breaking*; the current landscape is surveyed in Butler et al., 2023, *Report of the 2021 U.S. Community Study on the Future of Particle Physics*, arXiv:2301.06581.
solved_when: A predictive mechanism is identified that explains the Higgs mass's smallness relative to ultraviolet scales and yields observable consequences that distinguish it from unexplained parameter tuning, with experimental confirmation of those consequences.
why: A solution determines whether the Standard Model is part of a larger organizing structure, while continued failure leaves the electroweak scale's smallness an unexplained tuning.
key_works: Gerard ’t Hooft, 1980, *Naturalness, Chiral Symmetry, and Spontaneous Chiral Symmetry Breaking*; Butler et al., 2023, *Report of the 2021 U.S. Community Study on the Future of Particle Physics*, arXiv:2301.06581.

title: Higgs trilinear self-coupling
open: Measure the three-Higgs interaction precisely enough to distinguish the Standard Model potential from meaningful alternatives, without assuming away correlated new interactions.
status: Double-Higgs searches and indirect constraints currently provide only partial information on the coupling, and isolating it remains a major target for collider physics; the prospects have been studied by Maura, Stefanek, and You, 2025, *The Higgs Self-Coupling at FCC-ee*, arXiv:2503.13719.
solved_when: The Higgs trilinear self-coupling is determined with sufficient precision — as targeted at future colliders such as the FCC-ee — to discriminate the Standard Model Higgs potential from meaningful alternative scenarios, with correlated new interactions consistently disentangled rather than assumed absent.
why: The measurement tests the shape of the Higgs potential and probes whether the electroweak phase transition could have been qualitatively different from the Standard Model expectation.
key_works: Maura, Stefanek, and You, 2025, *The Higgs Self-Coupling at FCC-ee*, arXiv:2503.13719.

title: Origin of fermion masses and mixing
open: Can the observed quark and lepton mass hierarchies and mixing matrices be derived from a predictive underlying structure, rather than treated as independent fitted inputs? In formal terms, is there a framework whose symmetry or texture structure fixes these observables with fewer free parameters than the Standard Model itself?
status: Flavor symmetries and texture models have existed for decades, and many reproduce subsets of the data; however, no uniquely established predictive explanation exists. Key works include Froggatt and Nielsen, 1979, *Hierarchy of Quark Masses, Cabibbo Angles and CP Violation*; de Gouvêa et al., 2022, *Theory of Neutrino Physics*, arXiv:2209.07983.
solved_when: A single predictive framework reproduces the observed quark and lepton mass hierarchies and mixing matrices, with no uniquely established alternative remaining — i.e., a unique predictive explanation exists rather than models that merely reproduce subsets of data.
why: It would explain a large fraction of the Standard Model's unexplained parameters, replacing fitted inputs with derived structure.
key_works: Froggatt and Nielsen, 1979, *Hierarchy of Quark Masses, Cabibbo Angles and CP Violation*; de Gouvêa et al., 2022, *Theory of Neutrino Physics*, arXiv:2209.07983.

title: Proton decay
open: Can we observe the decay of a proton, or prove that specified grand-unified models are wrong by bounding how long the proton lives channel by channel? Formally, the goal is either a baryon-number-violating signal or channel-resolved lifetime limits with controlled backgrounds that exclude those models.
status: Searches extend over decades and have found no accepted signal. Different unification models predict different dominant channels and lifetimes. Key works: Langacker, 1981, *Grand Unified Theories and Proton Decay*; Butler et al., 2023, arXiv:2301.06581.
solved_when: Either an accepted observation of baryon-number-violating proton decay is made, or channel-resolved proton lifetime bounds with controlled backgrounds are established that exclude the specified grand-unified models.
why: A result either way tests whether baryon number is fundamentally conserved and whether the forces unify.
key_works: Langacker, 1981, *Grand Unified Theories and Proton Decay*; Butler et al., 2023, arXiv:2301.06581.

title: Muon g−2 hadronic-prediction reconciliation
open: Reconcile dispersive, lattice, and experimental hadronic inputs into a mutually consistent Standard Model prediction whose uncertainty supports a reliable comparison with the measured muon magnetic moment.
status: Fermilab completed its final measurement in 2025. Updated theory changes the interpretation: the problem should not be described as an unchanged, established earlier-significance discrepancy.
why: Determines whether an exceptionally precise observable reveals new physics or unresolved strong-interaction inputs.
key_works: Muon g−2 Theory Initiative, 2025 update; Fermilab Muon g−2 Collaboration, 2025 final measurement materials.

title: Leptonic CP violation
open: Does the lepton sector exhibit CP violation in neutrino oscillations, and if so, what is the value of the CP-violating phase? A convincing measurement must isolate a genuine intrinsic asymmetry from matter effects and interaction-model errors.
